provisions.name: 10. Mortgage Insurance
provisions.text:
10. Mortgage Insurance. If Lender required Mortgage Insurance as a condition of making the Loan, Borrower shall pay the premiums required to maintain the Mortgage Insurance in effect. If, for any reason, the Mortgage Insurance coverage required by Lender ceases to be available from the mortgage insurer that previously provided such insurance and Borrower was required to make separately designated payments toward the premiums for Mortgage Insurance, Borrower shall pay the premiums required to obtain coverage substantially equivalent to the Mortgage Insurance previously in effect, at a cost substantially equivalent to the cost to Borrower of the Mortgage Insurance previously in effect, from an alternate mortgage insurer approved by Lender. If substantially equivalent Mortgage Insurance coverage is not available, Borrower shall continue to pay to Lender the amount of the separately designated payments that were due when the insurance coverage ceased to be in effect. Lender will accept, use and retain these payments as a non-refundable loss reserve in lieu of Mortgage Insurance. Such loss reserve shall be non-refundable, notwithstanding the fact that the Loan is ultimately paid in full, and Lender shall not be required to pay Borrower any interest or earnings on such loss reserve. Lender can no longer require loss reserve payments if Mortgage Insurance coverage (in the amount and for the period that Lender requires) provided by an insurer selected by Lender again becomes available, is obtained, and Lender requires separately designated payments toward the premiums for Mortgage Insurance. If Lender required Mortgage Insurance as a condition of making the Loan and Borrower was required to make separately designated payments toward the premiums for Mortgage Insurance, Borrower shall pay the premiums required to maintain Mortgage Insurance in effect, or to provide a non-refundable loss reserve, until Lender's requirement for Mortgage Insurance ends in accordance with any written agreement between Borrower and Lender providing for such termination or until termination is required by Applicable Law. Nothing in this Section 10 affects Borrower's obligation to pay interest at the rate provided in the Note.

Mortgage Insurance reimburses Lender (or any entity that purchases the Note) for certain losses it may incur if Borrower does not repay the Loan as agreed. Borrower is not a party to the Mortgage Insurance.

Mortgage insurers evaluate their total risk on all such insurance in force from time to time, and may enter into agreements with other parties that share or modify their risk, or reduce losses. These agreements are on terms and conditions that are satisfactory to the mortgage insurer and the other party (or parties) to these agreements. These agreements may require the mortgage insurer to make payments using any source of funds that the mortgage insurer may have available (which may include funds obtained from Mortgage Insurance premiums).

As a result of these agreements, Lender, any purchaser of the Note, another insurer, any reinsurer, any other entity, or any affiliate of any of the foregoing, may receive (directly or indirectly) amounts that derive from (or might be characterized as) a portion of Borrower's payments for Mortgage Insurance, in exchange for sharing or modifying the mortgage insurer's risk, or reducing losses. If such agreement provides that an affiliate of Lender takes a share of the insurer's risk in exchange for a share of the premiums paid to the insurer, the arrangement is often termed "captive reinsurance." Further:

(a) Any such agreements will not affect the amounts that Borrower has agreed to pay for Mortgage Insurance, or any other terms of the Loan. Such agreements will not increase the amount Borrower will owe for Mortgage Insurance, and they will not entitle Borrower to any refund.

(b) Any such agreements will not affect the rights Borrower has - if any - with respect to the Mortgage Insurance under the Homeowners Protection Act of 1998 or any other law. These rights may include the right to receive certain disclosures, to request and obtain cancellation of the Mortgage Insurance, to have the Mortgage Insurance terminated automatically, and/or to receive a refund of any Mortgage Insurance premiums that were unearned at the time of such cancellation or termination.

provisions.name: 11. Assignment of Miscellaneous Proceeds; Forfeiture
provisions.text:
11. Assignment of Miscellaneous Proceeds; Forfeiture. All Miscellaneous Proceeds are hereby assigned to and shall be paid to Lender.

If the Property is damaged, such Miscellaneous Proceeds shall be applied to restoration or repair of the Property, if the restoration or repair is economically feasible and Lender's security is not lessened. During such repair and restoration period, Lender shall have the right to hold such Miscellaneous Proceeds until Lender has had an opportunity to inspect such Property to ensure the work has been completed to Lender's satisfaction, provided that such inspection shall be undertaken promptly. Lender may pay for the repairs and restoration in a single disbursement or in a series of progress payments as the work is completed. Unless an agreement is made in writing or Applicable Law requires interest to be paid on such Miscellaneous Proceeds, Lender shall not be required to pay Borrower any interest or earnings on such Miscellaneous Proceeds. If the restoration or repair is not economically feasible or Lender's security would be lessened, the Miscellaneous Proceeds shall be applied to the sums secured by this Security Instrument, whether or not then due, with the excess, if any, paid to Borrower. Such Miscellaneous Proceeds shall be applied in the order provided for in Section 2.

In the event of a total taking, destruction, or loss in value of the Property, the Miscellaneous Proceeds shall be applied to the sums secured by this Security Instrument, whether or not then due, with the excess, if any, paid to Borrower.

In the event of a partial taking, destruction, or loss in value of the Property in which the fair market value of the Property immediately before the partial taking, destruction, or loss in value is equal to or greater than the amount of the sums secured by this Security Instrument immediately before the partial taking, destruction, or loss in value, unless Borrower and Lender otherwise agree in writing, the sums secured by this Security Instrument shall be reduced by the amount of the Miscellaneous Proceeds multiplied by the following fraction: (a) the total amount of the sums secured immediately before the partial taking, destruction, or loss in value divided by (b) the fair market value of the Property immediately before the partial taking, destruction, or loss in value. Any balance shall be paid to Borrower.

In the event of a partial taking, destruction, or loss in value of the Property in which the fair market value of the Property immediately before the partial taking, destruction, or loss in value is less than the amount of the sums secured immediately before the partial taking, destruction, or loss in value, unless Borrower and Lender otherwise agree in writing, the Miscellaneous Proceeds shall be applied to the sums secured by this Security Instrument whether or not the sums are then due.

If the Property is abandoned by Borrower, or if, after notice by Lender to Borrower that the Opposing Party (as defined in the next sentence) offers to make an award to settle a claim for damages, Borrower fails to respond to Lender within 30 days after the date the notice is given, Lender is authorized to collect and apply the Miscellaneous Proceeds either to restoration or repair of the Property or to the sums secured by this Security Instrument, whether or not then due. "Opposing Party" means the third party that owes Borrower Miscellaneous Proceeds or the party against whom Borrower has a right of action in regard to Miscellaneous Proceeds.

Borrower shall be in default if any action or proceeding, whether civil or criminal, is begun that, in Lender's judgment, could result in forfeiture of the Property or other material impairment of Lender's interest in the Property or rights under this Security Instrument. Borrower can cure such a default and, if acceleration has occurred, reinstate as provided in Section 19, by causing the action or proceeding to be dismissed with a ruling that, in Lender's judgment, precludes forfeiture of the Property or other material impairment of Lender's interest in the Property or rights under this Security Instrument. The proceeds of any award or claim for damages that are attributable to the impairment of Lender's interest in the Property are hereby assigned and shall be paid to Lender.

All Miscellaneous Proceeds that are not applied to restoration or repair of the Property shall be applied in the order provided for in Section 2.

provisions.name: 12. Borrower Not Released; Forbearance By Lender Not a Waiver
provisions.text: 12. **Borrower Not Released; Forbearance By Lender Not a Waiver.** Extension of the time for payment or modification of amortization of the sums secured by this Security Instrument granted by Lender to Borrower or any Successor in Interest of Borrower shall not operate to release the liability of Borrower or any Successors in Interest of Borrower. Lender shall not be required to commence proceedings against any Successor in Interest of Borrower or to refuse to extend time for payment or otherwise modify amortization of the sums secured by this Security Instrument by reason of any demand made by the original Borrower or any Successors in Interest of Borrower. Any forbearance by Lender in exercising any right or remedy including, without limitation, Lender's acceptance of payments from third persons, entities or Successors in Interest of Borrower or in amounts less than the amount then due, shall not be a waiver of or preclude the exercise of any right or remedy.

provisions.name: 13. Joint and Several Liability; Co-signers; Successors and Assigns Bound
provisions.text:
13. **Joint and Several Liability; Co-signers; Successors and Assigns Bound.** Borrower covenants and agrees that Borrower's obligations and liability shall be joint and several. However, any Borrower who co-signs this Security Instrument but does not execute the Note (a "co-signer"): (a) is co-signing this Security Instrument only to mortgage, grant and convey the co-signer's interest in the Property under the terms of this Security Instrument; (b) is not personally obligated to pay the sums secured by this Security Instrument; and (c) agrees that Lender and any other Borrower can agree to extend, modify, forbear or make any accommodations with regard to the terms of this Security Instrument or the Note without the co-signer's consent.

Subject to the provisions of Section 18, any Successor in Interest of Borrower who assumes Borrower's obligations under this Security Instrument in writing, and is approved by Lender, shall obtain all of Borrower's rights and benefits under this Security Instrument. Borrower shall not be released from Borrower's obligations and liability under this Security Instrument unless Lender agrees to such release in writing. The covenants and agreements of this Security Instrument shall bind (except as provided in Section 20) and benefit the successors and assigns of Lender.

provisions.name: 14. Loan Charges
provisions.text:
14. **Loan Charges.** Lender may charge Borrower fees for services performed in connection with Borrower's default, for the purpose of protecting Lender's interest in the Property and rights under this Security Instrument, including, but not limited to, attorneys' fees, property inspection and valuation fees. In regard to any other fees, the absence of express authority in this Security Instrument to charge a specific fee to Borrower shall not be construed as a prohibition on the charging of such fee. Lender may not charge fees that are expressly prohibited by this Security Instrument or by Applicable Law.

If the Loan is subject to a law which sets maximum loan charges, and that law is finally interpreted so that the interest or other loan charges collected or to be collected in connection with the Loan exceed the permitted limits, then: (a) any such loan charge shall be reduced by the amount necessary to reduce the charge to the permitted limit; and (b) any sums already collected from Borrower which exceeded permitted limits will be refunded to Borrower. Lender may choose to make this refund by reducing the principal owed under the Note or by making a direct payment to Borrower. If a refund reduces principal, the reduction will be treated as a partial prepayment without any prepayment charge (whether or not a prepayment charge is provided for under the Note). Borrower's acceptance of any such refund made by direct payment to Borrower will constitute a waiver of any right of action Borrower might have arising out of such overcharge.

provisions.name: 15. Notices
provisions.text: 15. **Notices.** All notices given by Borrower or Lender in connection with this Security Instrument must be in writing. Any notice to Borrower in connection with this Security Instrument shall be deemed to have been given to Borrower when mailed by first class mail or when actually delivered to Borrower's notice address if sent by other means. Notice to any one Borrower shall constitute notice to all Borrowers unless Applicable Law expressly requires otherwise. The notice address shall be the Property Address unless Borrower has designated a substitute notice address by notice to Lender. Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of Borrower's change of address. If Lender specifies a procedure for reporting Borrower's change of address, then Borrower shall only report a change of address through that specified procedure. There may be only one designated notice address under this Security Instrument at any one time. Any notice to Lender shall be given by delivering it or by mailing it by first class mail to Lender's address stated herein unless Lender has designated another address by notice to Borrower. Any notice in connection with this Security Instrument shall not be deemed to have been given to Lender until actually received by Lender. If any notice required by this Security Instrument is also required under Applicable Law, the Applicable Law requirement will satisfy the corresponding requirement under this Security Instrument.

provisions.name: 16. Governing Law; Severability; Rules of Construction
provisions.text:
16. **Governing Law; Severability; Rules of Construction.** This Security Instrument shall be governed by federal law and the law of the jurisdiction in which the Property is located. All rights and obligations contained in this Security Instrument are subject to any requirements and limitations of Applicable Law. Applicable Law might explicitly or implicitly allow the parties to agree by contract or it might be silent, but such silence shall not be construed as a prohibition against agreement by contract. In the event that any provision or clause of this Security Instrument or the Note conflicts with Applicable Law, such conflict shall not affect other provisions of this Security Instrument or the Note which can be given effect without the conflicting provision.

As used in this Security Instrument: (a) words of the masculine gender shall mean and include corresponding neuter words or words of the feminine gender; (b) words in the singular shall mean and include the plural and vice versa; and (c) the word "may" gives sole discretion without any obligation to take any action.

provisions.name: 17. Borrower's Copy
provisions.text: 17. **Borrower's Copy.** Borrower shall be given one copy of the Note and of this Security Instrument.

provisions.name: 18. Transfer of the Property or a Beneficial Interest in Borrower
provisions.text:
18. **Transfer of the Property or a Beneficial Interest in Borrower.** As used in this Section 18, "Interest in the Property" means any legal or beneficial interest in the Property, including, but not limited to, those beneficial interests transferred in a bond for deed, contract for deed, installment sales contract or escrow agreement, the intent of which is the transfer of title by Borrower at a future date to a purchaser.

If all or any part of the Property or any Interest in the Property is sold or transferred (or if Borrower is not a natural person and a beneficial interest in Borrower is sold or transferred) without Lender's prior written consent, Lender may require immediate payment in full of all sums secured by this Security Instrument. However, this option shall not be exercised by Lender if such exercise is prohibited by Applicable Law.

If Lender exercises this option, Lender shall give Borrower notice of acceleration. The notice shall provide a period of not less than 30 days from the date the notice is given in accordance with Section 15 within which Borrower must pay all sums secured by this Security Instrument. If Borrower fails to pay those sums prior to the expiration of this period, Lender may invoke any remedies permitted by this Security Instrument without further notice or demand on Borrower.

provisions.name: 19. Borrower's Right to Reinstate After Acceleration
provisions.text: 19. **Borrower's Right to Reinstate After Acceleration.** If Borrower meets certain conditions, Borrower shall have the right to have enforcement of this Security Instrument discontinued at any time prior to the earliest of: (a) five days before sale of the Property pursuant to any power of sale contained in this Security Instrument; (b) such other period as Applicable Law might specify for the termination of Borrower's right to reinstate; or (c) entry of a judgment enforcing this Security Instrument. Those conditions are that Borrower: (a) pays Lender all sums which then would be due under this Security Instrument and the Note as if no acceleration had occurred; (b) cures any default of any other covenants or agreements; (c) pays all expenses incurred in enforcing this Security Instrument, including, but not limited to, Reasonable Attorneys' Fees (as defined in Section 25), property inspection and valuation fees, and other fees incurred for the purpose of protecting Lender's interest in the Property and rights under this Security Instrument; and (d) takes such action as Lender may reasonably require to assure that Lender's interest in the Property and rights under this Security Instrument, and Borrower's obligation to pay the sums secured by this Security Instrument, shall continue unchanged. Lender may require that Borrower pay such reinstatement sums and expenses in one or more of the following forms, as selected by Lender: (a) cash; (b) money order; (c) certified check, bank check, treasurer's check or cashier's check, provided any such check is drawn upon an institution whose deposits are insured by a federal agency, instrumentality or entity; or (d) Electronic Funds Transfer. Upon reinstatement by Borrower, this Security Instrument and obligations secured hereby shall remain fully effective as if no acceleration had occurred. However, this right to reinstate shall not apply in the case of acceleration under Section 18.

provisions.name: 20. Sale of Note; Change of Loan Servicer; Notice of Grievance
provisions.text:
20. **Sale of Note; Change of Loan Servicer; Notice of Grievance.** The Note or a partial interest in the Note (together with this Security Instrument) can be sold one or more times without prior notice to Borrower. A sale might result in a change in the entity (known as the "Loan Servicer") that collects Periodic Payments due under the Note and this Security Instrument and performs other mortgage loan servicing obligations under the Note, this Security Instrument, and Applicable Law. There also might be one or more changes of the Loan Servicer unrelated to a sale of the Note. If there is a change of the Loan Servicer, Borrower will be given written notice of the change which will state the name and address of the new Loan Servicer, the address to which payments should be made and any other information RESPA requires in connection with a notice of transfer of servicing. If the Note is sold and thereafter the Loan is serviced by a Loan Servicer other than the purchaser of the Note, the mortgage loan servicing obligations to Borrower will remain with the Loan Servicer or be transferred to a successor Loan Servicer and are not assumed by the Note purchaser unless otherwise provided by the Note purchaser.

Neither Borrower nor Lender may commence, join, or be joined to any judicial action (as either an individual litigant or the member of a class) that arises from the other party's actions pursuant to this Security Instrument or that alleges that the other party has breached any provision of, or any duty owed by reason of, this Security Instrument, until such Borrower or Lender has notified the other party (with such notice given in compliance with the requirements of Section 15) of such alleged breach and afforded the other party hereto a reasonable period after the giving of such notice to take corrective action. If Applicable Law provides a time period which must elapse before certain action can be taken, that time period will be deemed to be reasonable for purposes of this paragraph. The notice of acceleration and opportunity to cure given to Borrower pursuant to Section 22 and the notice of acceleration given to Borrower pursuant to Section 18 shall be deemed to satisfy the notice and opportunity to take corrective action provisions of this Section 20.

provisions.name: 21. Hazardous Substances
provisions.text:
**21. Hazardous Substances.** As used in this Section 21: (a) "Hazardous Substances" are those substances defined as toxic or hazardous substances, pollutants, or wastes by Environmental Law and the following substances: gasoline, kerosene, other flammable or toxic petroleum products, toxic pesticides and herbicides, volatile solvents, materials containing asbestos or formaldehyde, and radioactive materials; (b) "Environmental Law" means federal laws and laws of the jurisdiction where the Property is located that relate to health, safety or environmental protection; (c) "Environmental Cleanup" includes any response action, remedial action, or removal action, as defined in Environmental Law; and (d) an "Environmental Condition" means a condition that can cause, contribute to, or otherwise trigger an Environmental Cleanup.

Borrower shall not cause or permit the presence, use, disposal, storage, or release of any Hazardous Substances, or threaten to release any Hazardous Substances, on or in the Property. Borrower shall not do, nor allow anyone else to do, anything affecting the Property (a) that is in violation of any Environmental Law, (b) which creates an Environmental Condition, or (c) which, due to the presence, use, or release of a Hazardous Substance, creates a condition that adversely affects the value of the Property. The preceding two sentences shall not apply to the presence, use, or storage on the Property of small quantities of Hazardous Substances that are generally recognized to be appropriate to normal residential uses and to maintenance of the Property (including, but not limited to, hazardous substances in consumer products).

Borrower shall promptly give Lender written notice of (a) any investigation, claim, demand, lawsuit or other action by any governmental or regulatory agency or private party involving the Property and any Hazardous Substance or Environmental Law of which Borrower has actual knowledge, (b) any Environmental Condition, including but not limited to, any spilling, leaking, discharge, release or threat of release of any Hazardous Substance, and (c) any condition caused by the presence, use or release of a Hazardous Substance which adversely affects the value of the Property. If Borrower learns, or is notified by any governmental or regulatory authority, or any private party, that any removal or other remediation of any Hazardous Substance affecting the Property is necessary, Borrower shall promptly take all necessary remedial actions in accordance with Environmental Law. Nothing herein shall create any obligation on Lender for an Environmental Cleanup.

provisions.name: 22. Acceleration; Remedies
provisions.text:
NON-UNIFORM COVENANTS. Borrower and Lender further covenant and agree as follows:

22. Acceleration; Remedies. Lender shall give notice to Borrower prior to acceleration following Borrower's breach of any covenant or agreement in this Security Instrument (but not prior to acceleration under Section 18 unless Applicable Law provides otherwise). The notice shall specify: (a) the default; (b) the action required to cure the default; (c) a date, not less than 30 days from the date the notice is given to Borrower, by which the default must be cured; and (d) that failure to cure the default on or before the date specified in the notice may result in acceleration of the sums secured by this Security Instrument and sale of the Property. The notice shall further inform Borrower of the right to reinstate after acceleration and the right to bring a court action to assert the non-existence of a default or any other defense of Borrower to acceleration and sale. If the default is not cured on or before the date specified in the notice, Lender at its option may require immediate payment in full of all sums secured by this Security Instrument without further demand and may invoke the power of sale and any other remedies permitted by Applicable Law. Lender shall be entitled to collect all expenses incurred in pursuing the remedies provided in this Section 22, including, but not limited to, Reasonable Attorneys' Fees (as defined in Section 25) and costs of title evidence.

If Lender invokes the power of sale, Lender shall give notice of sale in the manner prescribed by Applicable Law to Borrower and to the other persons prescribed by Applicable Law. Lender shall publish the notice of sale, and the Property shall be sold in the manner prescribed by Applicable Law. Lender or its designee may purchase the Property at any sale. The proceeds of the sale shall be applied in the following order: (a) to all expenses of the sale, including, but not limited to, Reasonable Attorneys' Fees (as defined in Section 25); (b) to all sums secured by this Security Instrument; and (c) any excess to the clerk of the circuit court of the county in which the sale is held.

provisions.name: 23. Release
provisions.text: 23. Release. Upon payment of all sums secured by this Security Instrument, Lender shall release this Security Instrument. Borrower shall pay any recitation costs. Lender may charge Borrower a fee for releasing this Security Instrument, but only if the fee is paid to a third party for services rendered and the charging of the fee is permitted under Applicable Law.

provisions.name: 24. Accelerated Redemption Periods
provisions.text: 24. Accelerated Redemption Periods. If the Property is a one- to four-family residence that is owner-occupied at the commencement of a foreclosure, a farm, a church or owned by a tax exempt charitable organization, Borrower agrees to the provisions of Section 846.101 of the Wisconsin Statutes, and as the same may be amended or renumbered from time to time, permitting Lender, upon waiving the right to judgment for deficiency, to hold the foreclosure sale of real estate of 20 acres or less six months after a foreclosure judgment is entered. If the Property is other than a one- to four-family residence that is owner-occupied at the commencement of a foreclosure, a farm, a church, or a tax-exempt charitable organization, Borrower agrees to the provisions of Section 846.103 of the Wisconsin Statutes, and as the same may be amended or renumbered from time to time, permitting Lender, upon waiving the right to judgment for deficiency, to hold the foreclosure sale of real estate three months after a foreclosure judgment is entered.

provisions.name: 25. Attorneys' Fees
provisions.text: 25. Attorneys' Fees. If this Security Instrument is subject to Chapter 428 of the Wisconsin Statutes, "Reasonable Attorneys' Fees" shall mean only those attorneys' fees allowed by that Chapter.

provisions.name: 1. Definitions
provisions.text:
1. Definitions

(a) "Effective Date" shall refer to the date this Agreement is executed by both parties.

(b) "Termination Date" shall refer to the date this Agreement terminates.

(c) "Patent" shall refer to U.S. patent 7,125,398.

(d) "Product" shall encompass the needle guard to be manufactured under this License by Licensee or Licensee's manufacturer, arising under the medical needle guard as described in the Patent and the product design known as the Huber Safety Infusion Set provided to Licensee by Licensor. Product only includes devices that would infringe the Patent.

(e) "IP Rights" shall encompass U.S. Patent No. 7,125,398 and any reissues or continuations thereof.

(f) "Party to this Agreement" shall refer to Licensor and Licensee.

(g) "Validation Date" shall refer to the earlier of the following: (i) the date that validated and verified parts are supplied to Licensee from its manufacturer and those parts are accepted by Licensee to meet all drawing specifications provided to the manufacturer from Licensee, with Licensee to have no more than thirty (30) days to review and accept or reject parts after being so supplied; or (ii) June 1, 2012.

(h) "First Year" shall refer to a period from the Validation Date to the last day of the month falling 12 months after the Validation Date.

(i) "Second Year" shall refer to a one year period beginning on the last day of the month falling 12 months after the Validation Date to the last day of the month falling 24 months after the Validation Date.

(j) "Third Year" shall refer to a one year period beginning on the last day of the month falling 24 months after the Validation Date to the last day of the month falling 36 months after the Validation Date.

provisions.name: 2. Royalties, Quantity and Payments
provisions.text:
2. Royalties, Quantity and Payments

(a) The royalty rate is equal to $0.87 per sold unit of the Product sold by Licensee or its manufacturer (the "Royalty Rate").

(b) Licensee projects to manufacture at least 225,000 units of the Product in the First Year, and 262,500 units of the Product in the Second Year, and 325,000 units of the Product in the Third Year.

(c) Licensee agrees to notify Licensors in quarterly intervals the number of Products sold for the prior quarter.

(d) Licensee shall pay Licensors within 10 days after the end of the previous month the following: $16,313 each month for each of the 12 months of the First Year, $19,031 each month for each the 12 months of the Second Year, and $23,562 each month for each of the 12 months of the Third Year.

(e) At the end of each of the First Year, Second Year, and Third Year, Licensee shall pay Licensors an Excess Payment computed as the Royalty Rate multiplied by the number of Products sold in that year in excess of the projected amount for that year set forth in section (b) of this Section. For example, if, in the First Year, 230,000 Products were sold then at the end of the First Year, then the Licensee will make an Excess Payment of $4,350 to Licensors.

(f) At such point in time when at least $706,875 in the aggregate has been paid to Licensors by Licensee in accordance with this Section, then Sections (d) and (e) of this Section are no longer operative and instead Licensee will pay Licensors the Royalty Rate for each subsequent unit of the Product sold [in excess of aggregate 812,500 units for which payment had already been made] in quarterly intervals until the Termination Date.

(g) Past due amounts of royalties more than 30 days past due shall accrue interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is lower.

(h) Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the terms "sale", "sold", "sell", "purchase", "purchased", or similar words, when used in connection with a Product, shall mean any sale, conveyance, gift, assignment, or other transfer of any kind, whether with or without consideration, to any person or entity whatsoever.

(i) Licensee shall use good faith, best efforts to market and sell all Products manufactured.

(j) Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, in the event of termination of this Agreement and within thirty (30) days thereafter, Licensee shall pay to Licenser royalties at the Royalty Rate based upon all units of the Product purchased or ordered by Licensee, or otherwise in its possession and control that has not been included in previous royalty payments to licenser.

provisions.name: 3. Rights
provisions.text:

(a) Licenser hereby grants Licensee a non-exclusive, non-assignable license to the Licensee, during the term of this Agreement, to use the IP Rights for the purpose of manufacturing, advertising, and selling the Product in the U.S. and abroad, upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement (the "License"). Licensee may not make any other use of the IP Rights. Licensee shall notify Licenser in writing of the identity, contact information, and place of Product manufacture for each of Licensee's manufacturers. Under the License, Licensee's manufacturers so identified may manufacture Products for Licenser, but exclusively for Licensee, in accordance with and subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, with Licensee being responsible for its manufacturers' compliance with this Agreement.

(b) For each Product purchased by Licensee (or Licensee's permitted assigns or manufacturers) in accordance with this Agreement, the Licensee is free to dispose of that Product in any manner the Licensee wishes, including a sale (in U.S. or abroad), a gift or any other use.

provisions.name: 5. Indemnifications
provisions.text:
5. Indemnifications

(a) Licensors agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Licensee from any and against any and all claims, causes of action, damages, injuries, losses, expenses, attorneys fees, and harm of any kind relating to a third party claim against Licensee, to the proportional extent arising from Licensors material breach of this Agreement.

(b) Licensee agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Licensors from any and against any and all claims, causes of action, damages, injuries, losses, expenses, attorneys fees, and harm of any kind relating to a third party claim against Licensors, to the proportional extent arising from Licensors material breach of this Agreement.

(c) In event of a situation where both indemnification obligations apply, such indemnification will be comparative, based upon the respective fault of the parties.

(d) In event of a third party claim of patent infringement, then the monthly payments set forth in Section 2(d) are no longer required and Sections 2(e) and 2(f) will no longer be operative and instead Licensee will simply pay Licensors the royalty rate set forth in Section 2(a) for all sold items with no minimum quantities required until the earlier of the Termination Date or the date that such infringement claim is substantially resolved in favor of Licensors or Licensee.

provisions.name: 6. Patent Maintenance

Licensors will take, or cause Raul Garcia to take, all customary actions needed to maintain the validity of the Patent, such as paying maintenance fees when due, defending any reexaminations, and any other action needed to maintain the validity and enforceability of the Patent.

provisions.name: 7. Third party Infringements of the Patent

provisions.name: 8. New Product
provisions.text:

provisions.name: 9. Term
provisions.text:

(b) Upon termination of this Agreement for any reason, all rights and obligations set forth in this Agreement have terminated, although all Products purchased by Licensee under the terms of this Agreement before termination, and for which royalty payment has been timely made to Licensors, can still be sold, advertised, or distributed by Licensee with no restrictions whatsoever.

provisions.name: 10. Choice of Jurisdiction

provisions.name: 11. Assignment

11. Assignment

provisions.name: 12. Bankruptcy

provisions.name: 13. Entire Agreement
provisions.text:
13. Entire Agreement

If any section of this Agreement is found to be unenforceable by a court of law, all remaining sections of this Agreement remain valid and enforceable.

provisions.name: 14. Miscellaneous

(f) Licensor and Licensee acknowledge that each has had the full opportunity to read and review this Agreement prior to entering into it, and to consult with an attorney or waive their right to do so.

(g) Licensee makes no guarantees, representations, warranties, or promises regarding its sales activity of the Product and shall in its sole discretion devote as much or as little (or none) of its time and resources to selling the Product.

(h) If an improvement to the Product is discovered jointly by both Licensor and Licensee, then this improvement will become the property of Licensor. If such an improvement is discovered by Licensee without the contribution of Licensor, then this improvement will become the sole property of Licensee. If such an improvement is discovered by Licensor without the contribution of Licensee, then this improvement will become the sole property of Licensor.

(i) Should any party employ an attorney to enforce any of the provisions hereof, the non-prevailing party agrees to pay to the prevailing party all reasonable costs and expenses, including attorneys fees, incurred in connection therewith.

provisions.name: 17. Records/Audits
provisions.text:
17. Records/Audits

(a) Licensee shall maintain current, accurate and complete books and records relating to all payments due to Licensors pursuant to this Agreement, including without limitation manufacturing records. At any time during the term of this Agreement, and for a period of three (3) years after the termination of this Agreement, Licensee shall permit Licenser or Licenser's representative to examine, inspect, review and audit such books, records and copies and any source documents pertaining thereto. Such examination, inspection or audit shall take place during Licensee's normal business hours upon not less than three (3) business days' prior notice and shall not unreasonably interfere with Licensee's conduct of its business. Licenser or Licenser's designated representative may, at Licenser's expense, during the course of such examination, review or audit, make such copies and/or extracts of Licensee's books, records, copies and source documents that pertain to the royalties and other fees payable hereunder. Licenser's right to use a representative shall be subject to the execution by the representative of a confidentiality agreement reasonably proposed by Licensee in order to ensure that any confidential information disclosed thereby will be kept confidential and will be used only for the purposes of confirming Licenser's rights under this Agreement and ensuring compliance with the terms hereof by Licensee. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Licenser and its representative, if any, shall have the right to make reasonable inquiries and request documents of, and to receive prompt responses from, Licensee, at any time and from time to time, to confirm Licenser's rights under this Agreement and to ensure compliance with the terms hereof by Licensee. Should any audit reveal a payment shortfall of more than five percent (5%) of the amounts due to Licenser for any consecutive three-month period, Licensee shall reimburse Licenser for all direct costs of performing the audit. The amount of any shortfall (whether or not in excess of such percentage) shall be paid promptly following its discovery without interest. The amount of any overpayment shall, at Licenser's option, be refunded by Licenser to Licensee or credited against royalties payable by Licensee to Licenser.

(b) Licenser is limited to two requests under subsection (a) of this Section per year; provided, however, that an additional request is permitted in event a prior request during that year revealed a shortfall of more than five percent (5%) of the amounts due Licensee for any consecutive three-month period.

provisions.name: 2. Introduction
provisions.text:
# 2. INTRODUCTION

In order to provide for the future income security of its Employees, and in recognition of the valuable contribution made by its Employees, a pension plan is maintained for the benefit of Meriter Employees. Subsequent to the merger of Madison General Hospital and Methodist Hospital, the pension plans of both organizations were merged and a new pension plan was adopted effective as of October 1, 1987. The new plan attempts to preserve the best features of both of the prior plans. Special provisions apply under certain circumstances to Employees who were participants in the prior plans.

THE PLAN IS A LONG AND COMPLICATED DOCUMENT. IN AN EFFORT TO SIMPLIFY AND EXPLAIN THE PROVISIONS OF THE PLAN, CERTAIN DETAILS OF THE PLAN HAVE BEEN RESTATED OR OMITTED IN THIS SUMMARY. THEREFORE, IF YOU HAVE QUESTIONS ABOUT THE PLAN YOU SHOULD NOT RELY SOLELY ON THE FOLLOWING DESCRIPTION BUT SHOULD CONSULT THE PLAN DOCUMENT WHICH IS AVAILABLE AT THE PERSONNEL DEPARTMENT OF MERITER HOSPITAL OR ASK THE PLAN ADMINISTRATOR FOR FURTHER INFORMATION. YOUR RIGHTS AND BENEFITS UNDER THE PLAN ARE DETERMINED BY THE PROVISIONS OF THE PLAN AND NOT BY THE PROVISIONS OF THIS SUMMARY.

provisions.name: 3. Definitions (introduction)
provisions.text:
# 3. DEFINITIONS

The following terms that are used in this document are defined here for your convenience.

provisions.name: 3.1 Annual Earnings
provisions.text: **3.1 Annual Earnings** means the compensation paid to you by Meriter for that portion of the plan year in which you were a participant in the Plan, shown on your United States Treasury Form W-2, subject to certain modifications described in the Plan.

provisions.name: 3.2 Break in Service
provisions.text: **3.2 Break in Service** means a 12-consecutive month period which is used for eligibility or vesting purposes during which an Employee is credited with less than 501 Hours of Service.

provisions.name: 3.3 Effective Date
provisions.text: **3.3 Effective Date** means October 1, 1987.

provisions.name: 3.4 Employer
provisions.text: **3.4 Employer** means Meriter Health Services, Inc. and any related organizations that adopt this Plan.

provisions.name: 3.5 Hour of Service
provisions.text: **3.5 Hour of Service** means each hour for which an Employee is paid or entitled to payment. This includes regular time, overtime, vacations, holidays, illness, disability, and similar paid periods. There are limitations on the number of hours credited for such periods during which no duties are performed.

provisions.name: 3.6 Participant
provisions.text: **3.6 Participant** means an Employee who has satisfied the eligibility requirements for participation in the Plan and who makes required Employee contributions to the Plan.

provisions.name: 3.7 Plan Year
provisions.text: **3.7 Plan Year** means the calendar year from January 1 to December 31.

provisions.name: 3.8 Prior Defined Benefit Plan
provisions.text: **3.8 Prior Defined Benefit Plan** means the Madison General Hospital Pension Plan, General Medical Laboratories, Inc. Pension Plan, and General Health Management Co., Inc. Pension Plan.

provisions.name: 3.9 Prior Defined Contribution Plan
provisions.text: **3.9 Prior Defined Contribution Plan** means the Wisconsin Hospital Association Group Annuity Plan, Defined Contribution Plan, as adopted by Methodist Health Services, Inc., Methodist Health Foundation, Inc., Methodist Retirement Center, Inc., Methodist Hospital, and Allied Health Services, Inc.

provisions.name: 3.10 Prior Plan
provisions.text: **3.10 Prior Plan** means all Prior Defined Benefit Plans and Prior Defined Contribution Plans.

provisions.name: 3.11 Year of Service
provisions.text: **3.11 Year of Service** means a 12-consecutive month period during which an Employee is credited with at least 1,000 Hours of Service. In determining eligibility to participate in the Plan, the initial computation period is the 12-month period beginning on the first day of employment. For vesting and benefit accrual purposes, the 12-month period is the Plan Year.

provisions.name: 4.1.1 Eligibility
provisions.text: **4.1.1 Eligibility.** If you are age 21 or older and have completed at least 1000 Hours of Service with Meriter in either the 12-consecutive month period beginning on the date you were employed, or during any Plan Year thereafter, you are eligible to participate in the Plan. If you are a leased employee or are covered by a collective bargaining agreement with Meriter which does not provide for participation in the Plan, you are not eligible to participate in the Plan.

provisions.name: 4.1.2 Participation
provisions.text: **4.1.2 Participation.** If you were a participant in a Prior Plan and were employed on the Effective Date, you automatically became a Participant in the Plan on the Effective Date. If you were not a participant in a Prior Plan, and you met the eligibility requirements described in Section 4.1.1, you will become eligible to participate in the Plan on the next following April 1 or October 1 ("Participant Date"). For example, an Employee who met the eligibility requirements on February 26, 1993, would become eligible to participate on April 1, 1993; and an Employee who met the eligibility requirements on September 10, 1993, would become eligible to participate on October 1, 1993. If you do not elect to become a participant on the first Participation Date after you become eligible to participate, you may elect to become a Participant on any succeeding Participant Date assuming that you are still eligible to participate.

provisions.name: 4.1.3 Mandatory Employee Contributions
provisions.text: **4.1.3 Mandatory Employee Contributions.** Upon becoming eligible to participate, you must file with the Pension Committee a written election to participate and a written consent which authorizes the deduction from your paychecks of 1% of your Annual earnings ("Required Contributions") to the Plan. If you discontinue making your Required Contributions, you may not resume participation until the first Participation Date that is at least one year after the date you discontinued making your Required Contributions.

provisions.name: 4.1.4 Continued Participation
provisions.text: **4.1.4 Continued Participation.** You will continue to be a Participant in the Plan as long as you are employed by Meriter and continue to make your Required Contributions.

provisions.name: 4.2 Termination and Reemployment
provisions.text:
**4.2 Termination and Reemployment.** The rules regarding participation upon reemployment are complicated and you should contact the Plan Administrator for specific information regarding your situation. In general, if you were a Participant in the Plan at the time your employment terminated, you will participate in the Plan immediately upon reemployment if: (i) you had a vested benefit derived from Employer Contributions; or (ii) your period of Break in Service is less than the greater of five years or your Years of Eligibility Service before termination of employment. If you do not meet either of these conditions, or if you were not a Participant at the time your employment termination, then upon reemployment, you will be considered a new Employee for eligibility purposes.

For example, if you were a Participant prior to separation and had a vested benefit from Employer Contributions, you would become a Participant immediately upon reemployment regardless of the number of years you were separated from service, or the number of years of Eligibility Service you had earned previously. However, if you were a Participant prior to separation with four years of Eligibility Service, but did not have a vested benefit from Employer Contributions, and then incurred five or more consecutive one-year Breaks in Service, you would be considered a new Employee for eligibility purposes.

provisions.name: 4.3 Prior Plan Service
provisions.text: **4.3 Prior Plan Service.** Your Years of Service under a Prior Defined Benefit Plan (Madison General Plan) or a Prior Defined Contribution Plan (Methodist Plan) are counted in determining Eligibility Service under the Plan.

provisions.name: 5.1 Pension Benefit Calculations
provisions.text:
**5.1 Pension Benefit Calculations.** The amount of your Pension benefit will be determined by your Account Balance at the time you retire. Your Account Balance consists of your Required Contributions, Meriter's Contributions, and the earnings credited to your Account. If you participated in the Madison General Plan or Methodist Plan, you will also receive credit for the benefits earned under Those Plans as of the Effective Date.

Each year that you participate in the Plan, your Account will be credited with a Yearly Accrual equal to 6% of your Annual Earnings (1% from your Required Contributions, and 5% from Meriter's Contributions). If you have ten or more years of Vesting Service (including the current year), the amount of the Yearly Accrual is increased to 7.5% of your Annual Earnings (1% from your Required Contributions and 6.5% from Meriter's Contributions).

Your Account will also be increased each year by an Investment Credit. The amount of the Investment Credit is computed differently on the amounts you contributed to the Plan and the amounts that Meriter contributed. The amount credited on your contributions to the Madison General Pension Plan prior to January 1, 1988 was 5% per year. After January 1, 1988, this rate and the rate credited on your contributions to the Methodist Pension Plan, were changed to the greater of 120% of the Federal Mid-term Rate (published by the Internal Revenue Service) or the Indexing Rate. The Indexing Rate is the rate of return credited on Meriter's contributions to the Plan which is determined each year by the Pension Committee. This rate will not be less than 4% per year.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break at "ten or more years of / Vesting Service".

provisions.name: 5.2 Benefits from the Madison General Pension Plan
provisions.text: **5.2 Benefits from the Madison General Pension Plan.** If you were a participant in the Madison General Pension Plan, your Account Balance will be credited with your accrued benefit as determined under the Pension Plan as of October 1, 1987. In addition, if you were a participant in the Madison General Pension Plan on September 30, 1987 and were making contributions to the Plan, your Account will be credited with a special Transition Credit. The amount of this credit is the sum of: (i) your contributions to the Plan as of October 1, 1987 plus interest at 12% per year; and (ii) the excess, if any, of three times the amount computed in (i) over the single sum equivalent of your accrued benefit under the Plan as of October 1, 1987. For example, if your contributions to the Plan as of October 1, 1987 were $2,000 including interest, and the single sum equivalent of your accrued benefit was $5,000, your Transition Credit would be (i) $2,000 plus (ii) three times $2,000 minus $5,000 which equals $1,000, for a total of $3,000.
provisions.repairs: Removed escape backslashes before dollar signs.

provisions.name: 5.3 Benefits from the Methodist Pension Plan
provisions.text: **5.3 Benefits from the Methodist Pension Plan.** If you were a participant in the Methodist Pension Plan, your Account Balance will be credited with the amount of your Account Balance under the Methodist Plan as of October 1, 1987.

provisions.name: 5.4 Separation from Service Prior to October 1, 1987
provisions.text: **5.4 Separation from Service Prior to October 1, 1987.** If you separated from service prior to October 1, 1987 and were receiving benefits from a Prior Plan, you will continue to receive benefits in the same form and amount as you had elected under the Prior Plan. If you separated from service with a deferred vested benefit under a Prior Plan, you continue to be entitled to receive the same benefits you were entitled to receive under the Prior Plan.

provisions.name: 5.5 Termination and Reemployment
provisions.text: **5.5 Termination and Reemployment.** The rules regarding computation of benefits upon reemployment are very complicated. You should contact the Plan Administrator for specific information on your situation. Your benefits will depend upon factors such as when you terminated employment, whether or not you had a vested benefit at the time of termination, how long you were gone, and the actions that you take upon reemployment.

provisions.name: 6.1 General Distribution Rules
provisions.text: **6.1 General Distribution Rules.** You may receive a distribution of benefits upon termination of employment due to normal retirement, postponed retirement, disability retirement or separation from service. Your beneficiary is entitled to receive your benefits upon your death. Benefits may also be distributed to a former spouse of a Participant pursuant to a qualified domestic relations order. A qualified domestic relations order is an order entered in a divorce proceeding which requires the Trustee to distribute benefits to a Participant's former spouse. Distributions you receive from the Plan are subject to income tax. You should discuss the tax consequences of receiving benefits with your tax advisor.

provisions.name: 6.1.1 Normal Retirement
provisions.text: **6.1.1 Normal Retirement.** Normal Retirement Age under the Plan is age 65. You are entitled to begin to receive your benefits not later than the first day of the month after you reach age 65.

provisions.name: 6.1.2 Early Retirement
provisions.text: **6.1.2 Early Retirement.** Early retirement benefits are payable if you retire after reaching age 55. The amount of the benefit, however, is reduced because the benefits will be paid to you over a longer period of time. For Plan Years beginning after December 31, 1988, normal retirement benefits are reduced by 2% for each year (2/12th% per month) that you retire prior to normal retirement. Prior to January 1, 1989, the retirement benefits were reduced by 5% per year for retirement between ages 60 and 65 plus an additional 3% per year for retirement between ages 55 and 60. For example, if you retire at age 62, after December 31, 1988, and your normal retirement benefit is $500 per month, your monthly benefit will be reduced by 6% (2% times 3) resulting in a benefit of $500 minus 6% times $500 equals $470 per month.
provisions.repairs: Removed escape backslashes before dollar signs.

provisions.name: 6.1.3 Postponed Retirement
provisions.text: **6.1.3 Postponed Retirement.** If you continue to work for Meriter after normal retirement age, and continue to make your Required Contributions, your account will continue to be credited with Yearly Accruals and interest accruals until you retire. Pension benefits will become payable to you when you retire. If you continue employment beyond age 70 1/2, benefits must begin to be paid to you even though you continue to be employed by Meriter.

provisions.name: 6.1.4 Disability Retirement
provisions.text: **6.1.4 Disability Retirement.** If you become disabled while employed by Meriter, your benefits are fully vested regardless of your years of vesting service. You will be eligible to receive a disability retirement pension beginning on the first day of the month after you reach normal retirement age. The requirement that you make contributions to the Plan is waived during the period you are disabled. Yearly Accruals and interest accruals continue to be credited to your account based on your earnings at the time you became disabled.

provisions.name: 6.1.5 Separation From Service
provisions.text:
**6.1.5 Separation From Service.** If you leave employment with Meriter, the amount of benefits you are entitled to receive will depend upon your vested interest in your account balance. Vesting refers to your ownership rights in your account balance.

You are always 100% vested in your Mandatory Contributions to the Plan and in the earnings credited on your contributions. You have the right to receive a distribution of these contributions and earnings at anytime after you separate from service.

On the amounts contributed by Meriter, you earn one year of vesting service for each Plan Year that you are credited with at least 1000 hours of service and contribute to the Plan. After you have earned 5 years of vesting service, your account balance including the amount contributed by Meriter and the earnings on the Meriter Contributions, becomes fully vested. If you terminate employment prior to being credited with 5 years of vesting service, you will have no vested interest in the Meriter Contributions or earnings on the Meriter Contributions credited to your account.

If you participated in a Prior Plan, all of your years of Participation in the Prior Plan are counted toward the vesting requirements under the new Plan. A special rule applies if you are credited with less than 5 years of vesting service and had been a participant in the prior Methodist Plan. Under these circumstances, the vesting schedule of that Plan still applies to Meriter's Contributions. However, after you are credited with a total of 5 years of vesting service under the Methodist Plan and the new Plan, you will be 100% vested in all of the contributions.

provisions.name: 6.2 Death Benefits
provisions.text: **6.2 Death Benefits.** If you die before payment of your benefits begins, your entire account balance, including your contributions and Meriter's Contributions, is paid to your surviving spouse or other designated beneficiary.

provisions.name: 6.2.1 Payments to Spouse
provisions.text: **6.2.1 Payments to Spouse.** If you were married at the time of your death, under normal circumstances your Plan benefits will be paid to your surviving spouse. If you were not married, or your spouse has consented in writing to your naming another beneficiary, payment will be made to your named beneficiary.

provisions.name: 6.2.2 Beneficiary Designation
provisions.text: **6.2.2 Beneficiary Designation.** Forms are available from the Plan Administrator for you to name a beneficiary. For the beneficiary designation to be effective it must be filed with the Plan Administrator. A new beneficiary designation cancels all prior designations. The designation of a beneficiary other than your spouse must be approved by your spouse in writing on forms provided by the Plan Administrator and filed with the Plan Administrator. Your spouse's consent is irrevocable if given.

provisions.name: 6.3.1 Normal Form of Payment
provisions.text:
## **6.3 Method of Payment Upon Retirement.**

**6.3.1 Normal Form of Payment.** The Plan allows you to choose from a number of payment options upon retirement. If you are single when you begin to receive payments, your account balance normally will be converted to a life annuity under which you will receive equal monthly payments for the rest of your life. Upon your death, payment of benefits terminates. If you are married when you begin to receive benefits, your account balance normally will be converted into an annuity which provides for equal monthly payments to you for the rest of your life, and if you die before your spouse, your spouse will continue to receive 50% of your monthly payment for the rest of his or her life. The monthly payment that you would otherwise receive will be reduced to allow for the continued payments to your spouse after your death.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break at "The / monthly payment".

provisions.name: 6.3.2 Optional Forms of Payment
6.4 Method of Payment Upon Termination of Employment
provisions.text: **6.4 Method of Payment Upon Termination of Employment.** If you terminate employment with Meriter before reaching age 55, you may choose from a number of options for payment of your benefits.

provisions.name: 6.4.1 Nonvested Benefits
provisions.text: **6.4.1 Nonvested Benefits.** If your interest in Meriter's Contributions is not vested, and your contributions with interest total less than $3,500, your account balance will be paid to you in a lump sum. If your contributions and interest total more than $3,500, you may elect to leave the funds in the Plan where they will continue to accrue interest until distributed.
provisions.repairs: Removed escape backslashes before dollar signs.

provisions.name: 6.4.2 Vested Benefits
provisions.text: **6.4.2 Vested Benefits.** If your interest in Meriter's Contributions is vested, you may elect to leave the entire account balance in the Plan and continue to accrue interest. You also may elect to withdraw your account balance provided that you deposit the distribution (other than your Required Contributions) into an IRA or another employer's qualified retirement plan.

provisions.name: 6.5 Mandatory Distribution
provisions.text: **6.5 Mandatory Distribution.** If your account balance derived from Meriter Contributions and your Required Contributions is $3,500 or less, your vested benefits will be paid to you in a lump sum.
provisions.repairs: Removed escape backslash before dollar sign.

provisions.name: 6.6 Benefit Insurance
provisions.text:
**6.6 Benefit Insurance.** Benefits under this Plan are insured by the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) if the Plan terminates. Generally, the PBGC guarantees most vested normal retirement benefits, early retirement benefits, and certain disability and survivor's pensions. However, PBGC does not guarantee all types of benefits under covered plans, and the amount of benefit protection is subject to certain limitations.

The PBGC guarantees vested benefits at the level in effect on the date of plan termination. However, if a plan has been in effect less than 5 years before it terminates, or if benefits have been increased within the 5 years before plan termination, the whole amount of the plan's vested benefits or the benefit increase may not be guaranteed. In addition, there is a ceiling on the amount of monthly benefit that PBGC guarantees, which is adjusted periodically.

For more information on the PBGC insurance protection and its limitations, ask your Plan Administrator or the PBGC. Inquiries to the PBGC should be addressed to the Office of Communications, PBGC, 2020 K Street NW, Washington, DC 20006. The PBGC Office of Communications may also be reached by calling (202) 778-8800.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break at "the PBGC / guarantees".

provisions.name: 7.1 General Procedure
provisions.text:
# **7. CLAIMS PROCEDURE**

**7.1 General Procedure.** If you are filing a claim for benefits under the Plan, you must use the forms provided by the Plan Administrator. The Plan Administrator will notify you in writing of the disposition of your claim within 30 days after receipt of the claim. Any denial or partial denial of a claim will: (i) specify the reason or reasons for the denial; (ii) identify the Plan provisions on which denial is based; (iii) identify any additional material that may be necessary for you to perfect your claim and explain why such material is necessary; and (iv) explain the Plan's appeal procedure.

provisions.name: 7.2 Appeals
provisions.text: **7.2 Appeals.** You may appeal a denial of your claim under the Plan by filing a written request with the Plan Administrator within 60 days after the receipt of the Plan Administrator's denial or partial denial of your claim. The Plan Administrator must give you a full and fair review of your claim and allow you to review documents and to submit issues and comments in writing. The Plan Administrator may hire legal counsel to render legal advice in its review. Within 60 days after the receipt of your appeal, the Plan Administrator must render a decision on your appeal. The decision must include specific reasons for the decision, written in a manner which you can understand, with specific references to the Plan provisions on which the decision is based.

provisions.name: 8. Plan Termination
provisions.text:
# **8. PLAN TERMINATION**

Meriter has the right to terminate the Plan at anytime. Upon termination, you will become 100% vested in the present value of your accrued benefit, and benefits will be distributed to you in accordance with law. The assets of the trust fund will be allocated or divided among Participants and Beneficiaries in accordance with the following priorities:

- (i) To fund benefits for Retired Participants and their beneficiaries to whom payment commenced at least 3 years prior to the date of termination and Participants who could have retired and received payment of their benefits at least 3 years prior to the date of termination.
- (ii) To all benefits guaranteed and insured by the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC).
- (iii) To all other vested accrued benefits not insured by the PBGC.
- (iv) To all other accrued benefits provided under the Plan.

Any excess funds will revert to Meriter.

provisions.name: 9. Assignment of Benefits
provisions.text:
# **9. ASSIGNMENT OF BENEFITS**

Normally, you may not transfer or assign your interest in the Plan; that is, you may not sell it, use it as collateral, or otherwise give it away. Your creditors may not attach or garnish your interest in the Plan. However, the Plan Administrator may be required to use some or all of your benefits to pay court-ordered alimony, child support, or marital property rights to a spouse, former spouse, child or other dependent. The court order must follow a certain form and contain certain information. If it does not, the Administrator will not honor it. If it does, the Administrator must comply with it. The Administrator alone will determine whether the court order must be followed.

provisions.name: 10. Statement of ERISA Rights
provisions.text:
# **10. STATEMENT OF ERISA RIGHTS**

As a Participant in the Plan you are entitled to certain rights and protections under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). ERISA provides that all Plan Participants shall be entitled to:

- (i) Examine, without charge, at the Plan Administrator's office and at other specified locations, such as work sites and union halls, all Plan documents, including insurance contracts, collective bargaining agreements and copies of all documents filed by the Plan with the U.S. Department of Labor, such as detailed annual reports and plan descriptions.
- (ii) Obtain copies of all Plan documents and other Plan information upon written request to the Plan Administrator. The Administrator may make a reasonable charge for the copies.
- (iii) Receive a summary of the Plan's annual financial report. The Plan Administrator is required by law to furnish each Participant with a copy of this Summary Annual Report.
- (iv) Obtain a statement telling you whether you have a right to receive a pension at normal retirement age (age 65) and, if so, what your benefits would be at normal retirement age if you stop working under the Plan now. If you do not have a right to a pension, the statement will tell you how many more years you have to work to get a right to a pension. This statement must be requested in writing and is not required to be given more than once a year. The Plan Administrator must provide the statement free of charge.

In addition to creating rights for Plan Participants, ERISA imposes duties upon the people who are responsible for the operation of the employee benefit plan. The people who operate your Plan, called "fiduciaries" of the Plan, have a duty to do so prudently and in the interest of you and other Plan Participants and beneficiaries. No one, including your Employer, your union, or any other person, may fire you or otherwise discriminate against you in any way to prevent you from obtaining a pension benefit or exercising your rights under ERISA.

If your claim for a pension benefit is denied in whole or in part, you must receive a written explanation of the reason for the denial. You have the right to have the Plan Administrator review and reconsider your claim. Under ERISA, there are steps you can take to enforce the above rights. For instance, if you request materials from the Plan Administrator and do not receive them within 30 days, you may file suit in a federal court. In such case, the court may require the Plan Administrator to provide the materials and pay you up to $100 a day until you receive the materials, unless the materials were not sent because of reasons beyond the control of the Administrator.

If you have a claim for benefits which is denied or ignored, in whole or in part, you may file suit in a state or federal court. If it should happen that Plan fiduciaries misuse the Plan's money, or if you are discriminated against for asserting your rights, you may seek assistance from the U.S. Department of Labor, or you may file suit in a federal court. The court will decide who should pay court costs and legal fees. If you are successful the court may order the person you have sued to pay these costs and fees. If you lose, the court may order you to pay these costs and fees, for example, if it finds your claim is frivolous.

If you have any questions about your Plan, you should contact the Plan Administrator. If you have any questions about this statement or about your rights under ERISA, you should contact the nearest Area Office of the U.S. Labor-Management Services Administration, Department of Labor.

provisions.name: Recitals (Whereas clauses)
provisions.text:
WHEREAS, in September 2001, the MHS and MRS Boards of Directors established threshold goals for fundraising and apartment home pre-sales which were to be met prior to proceeding with the ground breaking for MainGate at Meriter Commons, and in January 2002 the Boards approved a plan of financing for the project; and

WHEREAS, due primarily to the downturn in the economy, those threshold goals were not achieved by the May 1, 2002, target date, with the Capital Campaign having raised $3,802,508 toward the $4,000,000 threshold goal and the Sales Team having pre-sold 32% of the life lease dollar value as compared to the 50% sales target; and

WHEREAS, upon further study of the market assumptions and forecast and further analysis of projections for fund raising and sales, management has determined that the project continues to be a financially viable, significant component of Meriter's senior housing development strategy; and

WHEREAS, various financing scenarios which would allow construction to begin prior to achieving the threshold goals and which result in acceptable financial ratios and financial performance were reviewed by the MRS Executive and Finance Committees on June 4, 2002; and

WHEREAS, management and the MRS Executive and Finance Committees also reviewed the risks of delaying the project, concluding that delay of MainGate past September 2002 will have negative implications for current donors, committed prospective residents, future pre-sales, project costs and project credibility, and also concluding that proceeding with construction will create a positive stimulus for additional donations and apartment sales; and

WHEREAS, management has prepared a revised business model, financing plan and financial proforma for consideration by the Boards of Directors of Meriter Health Services and Meriter Retirement Services; and

WHEREAS, the MHS Board of Directors has authorized the MHS Executive Committee to make decisions necessary to resolve any policy issues related to the MainGate project on behalf of the MHS Board of Directors and to approve a modified business model acceptable to both Meriter Health Services and Meriter Retirement Services;

provisions.name: Introduction
provisions.text:
## INTRODUCTION

The Meriter Health Services Employee Retirement Plan (the "Plan") represents an amendment and restatement of the Madison General Hospital Pension Plan. It is the Employer's intention that the Plan, as set forth herein, shall comply with the provisions of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, the Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act of 1982, the Tax Reform Act of 1984, the Retirement Equity Act of 1984, and the Tax Reform Act of 1986, including corresponding and other applicable provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended from time to time.

The Plan, as amended and restated effective as of January 1, 2003, or such other dates as are stated herein or as are required by law, reflects the applicable requirements of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (Uruguay Round Agreements Act), the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act of 1994, the Small Business Job Protection Act of 1996, the Taxpayer Relief Act of 1997, the Internal Revenue Service Restructuring and Reform Act of 1998, and the Community Renewal Tax Relief Act of 2000 (collectively referred to as "GUST") and the Economic Growth and Tax Relief Act of 2001 ("EGTRRA").

The Plan is intended to be a qualified defined benefit plan under Code section 401(a).

provisions.name: Article 1 – Definitions, introductory clause
provisions.text:
## ARTICLE I DEFINITIONS

The following words and phrases, as used herein, shall have the respective meanings set forth below, unless the context clearly indicates to the contrary:

provisions.name: 1.1 "Accrued Benefit"
provisions.text: 1.1 "Accrued Benefit", shall mean the Account Balance Accrued Benefit under Section 3.2, but in no case shall the Accrued Benefit be less than the Prior Accrued Benefit.

provisions.name: 1.2 "Actuarial Equivalent"
provisions.text: 1.2 "Actuarial Equivalent", except where specifically provided otherwise, shall mean of equivalent value computed using an interest rate of 6% and the Applicable Mortality Table.

provisions.name: 1.3 "Affiliated Entity"
provisions.text: 1.3 "Affiliated Entity" shall mean any entity within a related group of organizations as determined under Sections 414(b), (c), and (m) of the Code, regardless of whether such entity is participating in the Plan. For purposes of Section 3.16, Affiliated Entity status shall, in addition, be determined under Section 415(h) of the Code.

provisions.name: 1.4 "Annual Earnings"
provisions.text:
1.4 "Annual Earnings" shall mean the total compensation of an Employee for service performed for the Employer for the portion of the Plan Year that the Employee was a Participant in this Plan shown on the Employee's U.S. Treasury Form W-2 plus any amount contributed by the Employer pursuant to a salary reduction agreement which is not includable in the gross income of the Employee under Sections 125, 132(f), 402(a)(8), 402(h), 403(b), or 457 of the Code, but excluding payments for non-employment related services such as finder's fees, severance payments, worker's compensation payments, short-term disability payments, royalties, amounts contributed by the Employer to this Plan, reimbursement of expenses, and income imputed under the Code with respect to excess life insurance contributions by the Employer. Annual Earnings of a disabled Participant shall be calculated at the Participant's rate paid prior to any reduction in earnings clearly attributable to medical limitations that eventually result in total disability.

Effective for Plan Years beginning after December 31, 2001, the Annual Earnings of each Participant taken into account under the Plan for any year shall not exceed $200,000, as adjusted for cost-of-living increases in accordance with Section 401(a)(17)(B) of the Code.
provisions.repairs: Removed list bullets and the escape before the dollar sign.

provisions.name: 1.5 "Annuity Starting Date"
provisions.text: 1.5 "Annuity Starting Date" shall mean the first month for which a benefit is payable in the form of an annuity or any other form.

provisions.name: 1.6 "Beneficiary"
provisions.text: 1.6 "Beneficiary" shall mean the person last designated by a Participant on a form supplied by the Pension Committee as entitled to receive any benefits which may be payable under this Plan by reason of the death of the Participant before distribution of benefits to the Participant has commenced. If no such designation is in effect at the time of the death of the Participant, or if no person so designated survives the Participant, the Beneficiary shall be the spouse of the Participant or, if there is no spouse, the estate of the Participant. Designation of a person as Contingent Annuitant when the Contingent Annuitant Form of benefit payment has been elected or is applicable shall not constitute a designation of such person as Beneficiary with respect to any other benefit payable under this Plan.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence broken across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 1.7 "Board"
provisions.text: 1.7 "Board" shall mean the Board of Directors of the Employer.

provisions.name: 1.8 "Break in Service"
provisions.text: 1.8 "Break in Service" shall mean any Eligibility Computation Period, or Plan Year during which an Employee is credited with less than 501 Hours of Service.

provisions.name: 1.9 "Code"
provisions.text: 1.9 "Code" shall mean the Internal Revenue Code, as the same may be amended from time to time, and any regulations issued pursuant thereto as such law affects this Plan.

provisions.name: 1.10 "Contingent Annuitant"
provisions.text: 1.10 "Contingent Annuitant" shall mean the person last designated by a Participant on a form supplied by the Pension Committee as entitled to receive any benefits which may be payable under this Plan by reason of the death of the Participant after distribution of benefits to the Participant has commenced. If no such designation is in effect at the time of the death of the Participant, or if no person so designated survives the Participant, the Contingent Annuitant shall be the spouse of the Participant, or if there is no spouse, the estate of the Participant. Designation of a person as Beneficiary shall not constitute a designation of such person as Contingent Annuitant with respect to any benefit payable under this Plan.

provisions.name: 1.11 "Disabled"
provisions.text: 1.11 "Disabled" shall mean having incurred a disability which entitles a person to disabled worker's benefits in accordance with the Federal Social Security Act. For those Employees not administratively (as opposed to medically) eligible for Social Security total disability benefits, the criteria of Social Security total and permanent disability shall be applied by an independent physician selected by the Pension Committee.

provisions.name: 1.12 "Disability Retirement Date"
provisions.text: 1.12 "Disability Retirement Date" shall mean the date on which a Disabled Participant is eligible to receive a Disability Retirement Pension.

provisions.name: 1.13 "Disability Retirement Pension"
provisions.text: 1.13 "Disability Retirement Pension" shall mean the pension benefit payable to a Disabled Participant.

provisions.name: 1.14 "Early Retirement Date"
provisions.text: 1.14 "Early Retirement Date" shall mean the first day of the month on or after a Participant attains his 55th birthday.

provisions.name: 1.15 "Effective Date"
provisions.text: 1.15 "Effective Date" shall mean January 1, 2003.
