provisions.name: 1.16 "Eligibility Computation Period"
provisions.text: 1.16 "Eligibility Computation Period" shall mean, with respect to the initial Eligibility Computation Period, the twelve (12) consecutive month period beginning with the first day of the pay period in which the Employee first performs an Hour of Service for the Employer and ending on the last day of the pay period that includes the first anniversary of the last day of the pay period during which the Employee started work. Succeeding Eligibility Computation Periods commence with the first day of the pay period that includes the first day of the Plan Year which commences after the first day of the Employee's initial Eligibility Computation Period (regardless of whether or not the Employee is entitled to be credited with a year of Eligibility Service during the initial Eligibility Computation Period) and end on the last day of the pay period that includes the last day of the Plan Year. An Employee who is credited with a year of Eligibility Service in both the initial Eligibility Computation Period and the first Plan Year which commences after the first day of the Employee's initial Eligibility Computation Period shall be credited with two years of Eligibility Service.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the definition split across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 1.17 "Eligibility Service"
provisions.text: 1.17 "Eligibility Service" shall mean the sum of (i) an Employee's years of Eligibility Service in a Prior Plan as of December 31, 1986, plus, (ii) one year of Eligibility Service for each Plan Year commencing on or after January 1, 1987, during which an Employee completes at least 1,000 Hours of Service. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall an Employee's Eligibility Service earned during 1987 be less than the Eligibility Service such Employee earned under a Prior Plan from January 1, 1987, to the Effective Date.

provisions.name: 1.18 "Employee"
provisions.text: 1.18 "Employee" shall mean any person employed by the Employer who is receiving remuneration for personal services performed for the Employer, and who is not an independent contractor.

provisions.name: 1.19 "Employee Derivable Accrued Benefit"
provisions.text: 1.19 "Employee Derivable Accrued Benefit", for purposes of Section 3.16 as of any date of reference, shall mean a single life annuity commencing at the Participant's Normal Retirement Date Actuarially Equivalent to the amount of the Participant's accumulated contributions as of such date of reference projected to the Participant's Normal Retirement Date. Solely for purposes of this Section 1.19, Employee Contributions to a Prior Defined Benefit Plan shall be credited with a rate of interest equal to five percent (5%) per annum prior to January 1, 1988. Thereafter, Employee Contributions shall be credited with a rate of interest equal to either (i) one hundred twenty percent (120%) of the Federal Mid-Term Rate (as in effect under Section 1274 of the Internal Revenue Code on the first day of each Plan Year); or (ii) the Indexing Rate as defined in Section 1.29 for each Plan Year, whichever results in the greatest aggregate total. During the Plan Year in which employment is terminated, interest will be accrued based on the greater of four percent (4%) or one hundred twenty percent (120%) of the Federal Mid-Term Rate in effect on the first day of the Plan Year for each quarter of employment completed prior to termination. For purposes of this Section 1.19, Actuarially Equivalent is based on the Applicable Interest Rate and the Applicable Mortality Table.

provisions.name: 1.20 "Employer"
provisions.text: 1.20 "Employer" shall mean Meriter Health Services, Inc. or any successor thereto by merger, purchase, or otherwise, which shall adopt this Plan by action of its Board of Directors; and all Affiliated Entities which with the consent of Meriter Health Services, Inc., adopt this Plan for the benefit of their Employees. For the purposes of this Plan, Meriter Health Services, Inc., or any successor thereto, shall be the representative of any Affiliated Entities which become parties to this Plan and shall alone and in its own name take any action permitted to or required of the Employer hereunder, on behalf of itself and on behalf of such other organizations. The term "Employer" shall be construed in the singular or the plural as the context so allows.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the definition split across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 1.21 "Employer Contributions"
provisions.text: 1.21 "Employer Contributions" shall mean payments made by the Employer pursuant to the provisions of this Plan.

provisions.name: 1.22 "Employer Derivable Accrued Benefit"
provisions.text: 1.22 "Employer Derivable Accrued Benefit", for purposes of Section 3.16 as of any date of reference, shall mean the excess, if any, of the Participant's Accrued Benefit expressed as a single life annuity commencing at his Normal Retirement Date as of such date of reference over his Employee Derivable Accrued Benefit as of such date of reference.

provisions.name: 1.23 "Employment"
provisions.text: 1.23 "Employment" shall mean the service of an Employee with the Employer.

provisions.name: 1.24 "Enrolled Actuary"
provisions.text: 1.24 "Enrolled Actuary" shall mean an actuary selected by the Pension Committee or by the Employer who is enrolled by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries established under ERISA.

provisions.name: 1.25 "ERISA"
provisions.text: 1.25 "ERISA" shall mean the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as the same may be amended from time to time, and any regulations issued pursuant thereto as such law affects this Plan.

provisions.name: 1.26 "Fiduciary"
provisions.text:
1.26 "Fiduciary" shall mean any person who exercises discretionary authority or control over the management of the Plan, assets held under the Plan or disposition of Plan assets; who renders investment advice for direct or indirect compensation as to assets held under the Plan or has any authority or responsibility to do so; or who has any discretionary authority or responsibility in the administration of the Plan. For purposes of this Plan, the following are deemed to be Fiduciaries:

(A) The Trustee(s) to the extent it receives contributions hereunder, and

(B) Members of the Pension Committee.

In addition, any other person not listed who exercises authority or has responsibility of a fiduciary nature as described above and in Part 4 of Subtitle B of Title I of ERISA shall be considered a Fiduciary under this Plan.

provisions.name: 1.27 "Highly Compensated Employee"
provisions.text:
1.27 "Highly Compensated Employee" means—

(1) Effective for Plan Years beginning on or after January 1, 1997, subject to the provisions of Code section 414(q) and related Treasury Regulations, any Employee who—

(A) was a 5 percent owner (as defined in Code section 416(i)(1)) of the Employer or any Affiliate, at any time during the Plan Year or the preceding Plan Year; or

(B) for the preceding Plan Year:

(i) received compensation (as defined in Code section 414(q)(4)) from the Employer and all Affiliates in excess of $80,000 (as adjusted at the same time and in the same manner as under Code section 415(d), except that the base period shall be the calendar quarter ending September 30, 1996); and

(ii) if the Employer so elects, was in the top-paid 20 percent of Employees for such preceding Plan Year.

In determining who is a Highly Compensated Employee under this subsection (1), the following rules shall apply:

(I) An Employee is in the "top-paid 20 percent" of Employees for any Plan Year if he is in the group consisting of the top 20 percent of Employees, when ranked on the basis of compensation (as defined in Code section 414(q)(4)) paid for such Plan Year.

(II) For purposes of determining the number of Employees in the top-paid 20 percent of Employees under paragraph (B)(ii), the following Employees may be excluded:

(a) Employees who have not completed a six-month period of service;

(b) Employees who normally work fewer than 17½ hours per week;

(c) Employees who normally work not more than six months during the Plan Year;

(d) Employees who have not yet attained age 21; and

(e) to the extent allowable under applicable Treasury Regulations, Employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement between employee representatives and the Employer or any Affiliate.

(III) A former Employee shall be treated as a Highly Compensated Employee if he was a Highly Compensated Employee when he terminated employment with the Employer and all Affiliates or if he was a Highly Compensated Employee at any time after he attained age 55.

(IV) In determining whether an Employee is a Highly Compensated Employee for the Plan Year beginning on January 1, 1997, the amendments to Code section 414(q) made by Public Law 104-188, the Small Business Job Protection Act of 1996, as amended from time to time, shall be treated as having been in effect for the Plan Year beginning on January 1, 1996.
provisions.repairs: Removed markdown heading and list bullets and the escape before the dollar sign.

provisions.name: 1.28 "Hour of Service"
provisions.text:
1.28 "Hour of Service" shall mean each hour for which the Employee is paid by the Employer or entitled to payment

(A) for the performance of duties for the Employer during the applicable Plan Year, including each hour for which back pay, irrespective of mitigation of damages, has been either awarded or agreed to by the Employer, or

(B) on account of a period of time during which no duties are performed (irrespective of whether his employment has terminated) due to vacation, holiday, illness, incapacity (including disability), layoff, jury duty, military duty or leave of absence, excluding (a) each hour for which he is directly or indirectly paid, or entitled to payment on account of any such period for which such payment is made or due under a plan maintained solely to comply with applicable workers' compensation, or unemployment compensation or disability insurance laws and (b) each hour for which he is solely reimbursed for medical or medically related expenses he incurred. Hours credited with respect to any such period shall equal (and in no event exceed) the number of working hours regularly scheduled for a customary workweek or pro rata portion thereof, or if no working hours are regularly scheduled for a customary workweek 40 hours per workweek or pro rata portion thereof, subject to a maximum of 1,000 hours.

Hours of Service under this Section shall be determined and credited in accordance with Section 2530.200b-2 of the Department of Labor Regulations. Hours of Service shall be credited for any individual considered to be a leased employee for purposes of this Plan under Section 414(n) of the Code. Hours of Service shall be credited for employment with any Affiliated Employer, and transfer of employment between the Employer and Affiliated Employers, or between Affiliated Employers, shall be deemed to be continuous service for purposes of this Plan.

If an Employee is absent from work by reason of pregnancy, childbirth, adoption, or the care of such Employee's child immediately after birth or adoption, and if the absence begins on or after the Effective Date of this Plan, such Employee shall be credited, solely for purposes of avoiding a Break in Service, with sufficient Hours of Service in order to avoid a Break in Service in the Plan Year in which the absence begins; or, if the Employee already has sufficient Hours of Service to avoid a Break in Service in the Plan Year in which the absence begins, the Employee shall be credited solely with sufficient Hours of Service in order to avoid a Break in Service in the Plan Year immediately following the one in which the absence begins. Hours of Service during such absence shall be credited in an amount equal to Hours of Service the Employee would have had but for such absence or, if such hours cannot be determined, at the rate of eight hours per normal workday, but in no event shall more than 501 Hours of Service be credited under this paragraph during any single absence.

provisions.name: 1.29 "Indexing Rate"
provisions.text: 1.29 "Indexing Rate" shall mean a rate equal to the annual yield on 10-year Treasury Constant Maturities that is in effect for the November 30th preceding the Plan Year, but in no event less than four per cent (4%).

provisions.name: 1.30 "Late Retirement Date"
provisions.text: 1.30 "Late Retirement Date" shall mean any Retirement Date subsequent to the Normal Retirement Date determined in accordance with Section 3.11.

provisions.name: 1.31 "Limitation Year"
provisions.text: 1.31 "Limitation Year" shall mean the calendar year, January 1 through December 31.

provisions.name: 1.32 "Named Fiduciary"
provisions.text: 1.32 "Named Fiduciary" shall mean the members of the Pension Committee, or any successors thereto.

provisions.name: 1.33 "Normal Form"
provisions.text: 1.33 "Normal Form" shall mean the manner and period of pension payment payable determined in accordance with Section 3.12.

provisions.name: 1.34 "Normal Retirement Age"
provisions.text: 1.34 "Normal Retirement Age" shall mean the date the Participant attains age 65.

provisions.name: 1.35 "Normal Retirement Date"
provisions.text: 1.35 "Normal Retirement Date" shall mean the first day of the month subsequent to the month in which the Participant attains age 65.

provisions.name: 1.36 "Participant"
provisions.text: 1.36 "Participant" shall mean any Employee who has met the requirements of Article 2 and who has performed all acts required of him thereunder. Unless otherwise limited by the context, it shall include a former Employee who has retired and who is receiving benefits under this Plan, and a former Employee whose Employment has otherwise terminated after the Effective Date and who remains eligible for benefits hereunder in accordance with Article 6.

provisions.name: 1.37 "Participation Date"
provisions.text: 1.37 "Participation Date" shall mean the April 1 or October 1 after which an Employee has satisfied the requirements for eligibility to participate set forth in Article 2.

provisions.name: 1.38 "Pension Committee"
provisions.text: 1.38 "Pension Committee" shall mean the committee appointed by the Employer from time to time to supervise the operation and administration of the Plan as provided in Section 8.1. As of the Effective Date, this Committee is the Executive Compensation and Pension Committee.

provisions.name: 1.39 "Plan Administrator"
provisions.text: 1.39 "Plan Administrator" shall mean the Pension Committee.

provisions.name: 1.40 "Plan Year"
provisions.text: 1.40 "Plan Year" shall mean the calendar year, January 1 through December 31.

provisions.name: 1.41 "Prior Accrued Benefit"
provisions.text: 1.41 "Prior Accrued Benefit" shall mean the amount calculated under Section 1.1 of the Prior Plan with yearly Accruals ending 12/31/02 and indexing adjustments under Section 3.8 and Section 3.14 of the Prior Plan through the Participant's Normal Retirement Date or Late Retirement Date, if applicable.

provisions.name: 1.42 "Prior Plan"
provisions.text: 1.42 "Prior Plan" shall include the Meriter Health Services Employee Retirement Plan in effect on 12/31/2002.

provisions.name: 1.43 "Retirement Date"
provisions.text: 1.43 "Retirement Date" shall mean a Participant's Normal, Early, Late or Disability Retirement Date.

provisions.name: 1.44 "Single Sum Equivalent"
provisions.text: 1.44 "Single Sum Equivalent" shall mean the amount determined in accordance with Section 4.3.

provisions.name: 1.45 "Spouse"
provisions.text: 1.45 "Spouse" shall mean the person to whom a Participant is legally married as of the date of reference.

provisions.name: 1.46 "Termination Date"
provisions.text: 1.46 "Termination Date" shall mean the date on which the Participant ceases to be an Employee in accordance with the provisions of Article 6.

provisions.name: 1.47 "Vested Benefit"
provisions.text: 1.47 "Vested Benefit" shall mean that portion of the Participant's Accrued Benefit which is nonforfeitable in accordance with Article 6.

provisions.name: 1.48 "Vesting Service"
provisions.text:
1.48 "Vesting Service" shall mean each Plan Year in which the Employee completes at least 1,000 Hours of Service, except that in no event shall years of Vesting Service be credited for Plan Years prior to the Plan Year in which such Employee attained age 18.

In the case of a Participant who has five (5) or more consecutive one-Year Breaks in Service, the Participant's pre-break service will count in vesting the Employer-Derivable Accrued Benefit only if either:

(a) such Participant had a nonforfeitable interest in the Accrued Benefit attributable to Employer contributions at the time of separation from service, or (b) upon returning to service the number of consecutive one-Year Breaks in Service is less than the number of Years of Service accrued prior to the Breaks in Service.

provisions.name: 1.49 "Yearly Accrual"
provisions.text: 1.49 "Yearly Accrual" shall mean the amount determined in accordance with Section 3.8.

provisions.name: Construction of gender and number (unnumbered, Article 1)
provisions.text: The masculine gender, where appearing in the Plan, shall be deemed to include the feminine gender and the singular may include the plural, unless the context clearly indicates to the contrary.

provisions.name: 1.50 "Applicable Interest Rate"
provisions.text: 1.50 "Applicable Interest Rate" means for any Plan Year the annual interest rate of 30-year Treasury securities, as promulgated by the Treasury Department, for the month of December immediately preceding the Plan Year for which a calculation is made.

provisions.name: 1.51 "Applicable Mortality Table"
provisions.text: 1.51 "Applicable Mortality Table" means the mortality table prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury under IRC section 417(e)(3) adjusted to reflect no mortality prior to age 65.

provisions.name: 2.1 Eligibility
provisions.text:
2.1 Eligibility. Each Employee in the employ of the Employer on the Effective Date who was a Participant in the Plan shall be eligible to participate in this Plan on the Effective Date. All other Employees who have attained age 21 shall be eligible to participate as of the earlier of the April 1 or October 1 (the "Participation Date") following the anniversary of the first day of an Eligibility Computation Period in which the Employee is credited with at least 1,000 Hours of Service and provided:

(A) He is not a leased employee who may be excluded under Section 414(n) of the Code, or

(B) He is not covered by the terms of a collective bargaining agreement between the Employer and a bargaining representative of such person, unless such collective bargaining agreement specifically provides that he is eligible to participate in this Plan.

Employees who met the eligibility requirements of the Prior Plan but who chose not to contribute to the Prior Plan, and as a result were not Prior Plan Participants, become Plan Participants effective January 1, 2003. In the event that any questions arise as to the eligibility to participate in the Plan, they shall be decided in accordance with the provisions of Article 8.

provisions.name: 2.2 Leave of Absence
provisions.text: 2.2 Leave of Absence. Each Employee who, at the time he would otherwise have become a Participant, shall be absent from employment as a result of service in the Armed Forces or is on leave duly granted by the Employer or on lay-off for lack of work, shall become a Participant as of the Participation Date coincident with or next following the date on which such Employee shall have resumed his active Employment.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break.

provisions.name: 2.3 Reemployment
provisions.text: 2.3 Reemployment. A Participant who separates from service and is reemployed by the Employer, who had a vested benefit derived from Employer Contributions prior to incurring a Break in Service, or the number of whose consecutive one year Breaks in Service is less than the greater of five or the number of years of Eligibility Service which he had completed prior to his Break in Service, shall be eligible to participate in the Plan immediately upon his return to the employ of the Employer. A Participant who separates from service with the Employer and is reemployed by the Employer, who had no vested benefit derived from Employer Contributions prior to incurring a Break in Service, and the number of whose consecutive one year Breaks in Service is greater than the greater of five or the number of years of Eligibility Service which he had completed prior to his Break in Service, shall be considered a new Employee for eligibility purposes.

provisions.name: 2.4 Services With Another Employer
provisions.text: 2.4 Services With Another Employer. The Employer may grant past service credit to an Employee for employment with another employer performed prior to commencement of the Employee's employment for the Employer. Such past service credit may be given for purposes of determining the Employee's Eligibility Service and/or Vesting Service under the Plan. The granting of such past service credit is subject to action by the Plan Administrator to specify the prior employer and the purposes for which such service shall be credited. All employees of the prior employer shall be treated uniformly, and the granting of such past service credit shall be done in a manner that does not discriminate in favor of officers, shareholders, or highly compensated employees.

provisions.name: 3.1 Account Balance
provisions.text:
3.1 Account Balance – a record keeping account maintained solely for the purpose of determining the Participant's Account Balance Accrued Benefit. A Participant's Account Balance receives allocations of pay credits and interest credits under Section 3.4. A Participant's Account Balance does not represent a separately funded account, or an account into which assets are segregated for any Participant. As of 12/31/2002, a Participant's Account Balance equals (a) multiplied by (b), where (A) and (B) are defined below.

(A) The amount calculated under Section 1.1 of the Prior Plan, with indexing adjustments under Section 3.8 and Section 3.14 of the Prior Plan ending 12/31/2002.

(B) 8.0

provisions.name: 3.2 Account Balance Accrued Benefit
provisions.text: 3.2 Account Balance Accrued Benefit – a monthly single life annuity at the Participant's Normal Retirement Date. If the Participant's Annuity Starting Date is prior to his Normal Retirement Date, the Account Balance Accrued Benefit is calculated by taking the existing Account Balance, projecting such balance to the last complete calendar quarter preceding the Participant's Normal Retirement Date using the Indexing Rate that is in effect for the Plan Year containing the valuation date and converting that balance to an Account Balance Actuarial Equivalent single life annuity. If the Participant's Annuity Starting Date is on or after his Normal Retirement Date, the Participant's Account Balance is used in the calculation without any projection of future interest.

provisions.name: 3.3 Account Balance Actuarial Equivalent
provisions.text: 3.3 Account Balance Actuarial Equivalent – shall mean a benefit of equivalent value computed using the Applicable Mortality Table and Applicable Interest Rate.

provisions.name: 3.4 Credits to Account Balance
provisions.text:
3.4 Credits to Account Balance - A Participant's Account Balance will receive pay and interest credits, as provided in paragraphs (a) and (b) below.

(A) Pay Credit. Effective as of January 1, 2003, as of the end of each Plan Year during which a Participant was actively employed by an Employer, or as of the first day of the month coinciding with or next following the termination of a Participant's employment with an Employer, such person's Account Balance shall receive a pay credit equal to the percentage determined under the table below, multiplied by his Annual Earnings for the Plan Year, or by his Earnings for the portion of the Plan Year in which he is so employed. The applicable Pay Credit for any Plan Year is determined by the Participant's Vesting Service as of the last day of the current Plan year:

Years of Vesting Service | Annual Pay Credit
Fewer than 10 | 4.5%
10 to 19 | 6.0%
20 or more | 7.5%

(B) Interest Credit. As of the end of each Plan Year during which the Participant has an Account Balance Accrued Benefit, such Participant's Account Balance shall receive an interest credit equal to the Participant's Account Balance as of the preceding December 31, multiplied by the Indexing Rate for such Plan Year. Such interest credits shall continue beyond the date the Participant terminates employment and shall be prorated through the end of the last complete calendar quarter preceding the date the payment of the Participant's Account Balance Benefit commences.
provisions.repairs: Reduced the markdown table to plain rows.

provisions.name: 3.5 Normal Retirement Benefit
provisions.text: 3.5 Normal Retirement Benefit - A Participant retiring on or after reaching his Normal Retirement Date shall be entitled to receive his Accrued Benefit determined as of the date of his retirement. Such benefit shall be payable at the times, and to the extent and in the forms and manner available and subject to the rules set forth in Article 4.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break.

provisions.name: 3.6 Early Termination Benefit
provisions.text: 3.6 Early Termination Benefit – If a participant's employment with the Employer is terminated prior to his Normal Retirement Date but after completing at least 5 Years of Vesting Service, the Participant shall be entitled to receive his Accrued Benefit, determined as of the date of such termination of employment and commencing on his Normal Retirement Date. Alternatively, the participant may elect to commence monthly benefit payments as of the first day of any calendar month coincident with or next following the later to occur of the date of termination of employment or the effective date of the participant's application for benefits is filed with the Plan Administrator, where such benefit payments are Actuarially Equivalent to the Participant's Account Balance on the benefit commencement date. For purposes of this Section 3.6, Actuarial Equivalent shall mean the basis contained in Section 3.3. The form of any Early Termination Benefit payment is subject to the rules set forth in Article 4. In no case shall a Participant's Early Termination Benefit under this Plan be less than the early retirement benefit the Participant accrued under the Prior Plan with respect to his Prior Accrued Benefit.

provisions.name: 3.7 Death of Participant Prior to Commencement of Payment of Account Balance Accrued Benefit
provisions.text:
3.7 Death of Participant Prior to Commencement of Payment of Account Balance Accrued Benefit - If a Participant who is entitled to a Vested Benefit dies prior to the commencement of payment of his benefit:

(A) An amount equal to the Participant's entire Account Balance shall be paid in one lump sum to such Participant's Beneficiary as soon as is administratively practical after the Participant's death; provided however, if the Participant's Beneficiary is his surviving spouse, the Participant's entire Account Balance shall be paid to his surviving spouse in the form of an Actuarially Equivalent single life annuity commencing as soon as practical after the Participant's death; provided further, however, in lieu of the single life annuity described above, the Participant's surviving spouse may elect to receive an amount equal to the Participant's entire Account Balance, payable in one Actuarially Equivalent lump sum as soon as is administratively practicable after the Participant's death. For purposes of this Section 3.7, Actuarial Equivalent shall mean the actuarial basis contained in Section 3.3.

(B) Each Participant having an Account Balance may designate a Beneficiary or Beneficiaries to receive any payment or distribution which may be payable under the Plan upon his death by filing written notice in the manner prescribed by the Committee upon forms prescribed and furnished by it; provided, however, a married Participant's surviving spouse shall automatically be his Beneficiary and a married Participant may not designate any Beneficiary other than his spouse without the written consent of his spouse in accordance with the rules and regulations under Code Section 417.

(C) If the Participant dies leaving no surviving Beneficiary, an amount equal to the entire value of his Account Balance shall be distributed to the Participant's estate, in one lump sum cash payment, such distribution to be made as soon as practical after the date on which the Participant's death occurs, but in any event, not before the receipt by the Committee of all information and documents required to facilitate such distribution.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined subsection (B) across a page break and removed list bullets.

provisions.name: 3.8 Special Provisions for active Participants born prior to 1943 with 10 Years of Vesting Service on 12/31/2002
provisions.text:
3.8 Special Provisions for active Participants born prior to 1943 with 10 Years of Vesting Service on 12/31/2002 – The Account Balance Accrued Benefit for actively employed Participants born prior to 1943 with at least 10 Years of Vesting Service on 12/31/2002 shall not be less than the sum of (a) and (b) where (A) and (B) are:

(A) a monthly single life annuity at the Participant's Normal Retirement Date, calculated by taking the existing Fresh Start Account Balance, projecting such balance to the last complete calendar quarter preceding the Participant's Normal Retirement Date using the Indexing Rate that is in effect for the Plan Year containing the valuation date and converting that balance to an Account Balance Actuarial Equivalent single life annuity. For purposes of Section 3.8, Fresh Start Account Balance is a record keeping account maintained solely for determining a portion of a Participant's Accrued Benefit. A Participant's Fresh Start Account Balance receives allocations of pay credits and interest credits under Section 3.4. A Participant's Fresh Start Account Balance does not represent a separately funded account, or an account into which assets are segregated for any Participant. As of 12/31/2002 a Participant's Fresh Start Account Balance Account equals zero.

(B) Prior Accrued Benefit

provisions.name: 4.1 Normal Form of Benefit
provisions.text: 4.1 Normal Form of Benefit. The Normal Form of Benefit shall be a benefit payable monthly for the life of the Participant and commencing on the Participant's Normal Retirement Date, with the last payment due on the first day of the month in which the Participant's death occurs. In the case of a Participant who is married on his Annuity Starting Date, the payment of his retirement benefit shall be subject to the provisions of Section 4.2, relating to the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity.

provisions.name: 4.2 Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity
provisions.text:
4.2 Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity. If the Participant has a Spouse as of such date and does not elect an optional form of pension, his monthly amount of pension benefit shall be equal to the product of the 50% Contingent Annuitant Factor times the benefit determined in Section 3.12(A) with his Spouse as contingent annuitant being entitled, upon the Participant's prior death, to fifty percent (50%) of the pension payable to the Participant (a 50% "Joint and Survivor Annuity").

Notwithstanding the above, with respect to distributions made on or after December 31, 1996, if the Participant elects (with spousal consent) to waive the requirement that the explanation of the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity be provided at least 30 days before the Participant's Annuity Starting Date, the election period described in this section shall be extended to the 30th day after the date on which such explanation is provided to the Participant, unless the 30-day period is waived pursuant to the following provisions.

Any distribution of a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity made on or after December 31, 1996, may commence less than 30 days after the explanation required by this section \_\_ is furnished to the Participant, provided the following requirements are satisfied:

(A) The Plan Administrator clearly informs the Participant that he has a right to a period of 30 days after receiving the explanation to consider whether to waive the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity and to elect (with spousal consent) a form of distribution other than the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity;

(B) The Participant is permitted to revoke any affirmative distribution election at least until the Participant's Annuity Starting Date or, if later, at any time prior to the expiration of the 7-day period that begins the day after the explanation of the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity is provided to the Participant;

(C) The Participant's Annuity Starting Date is a date after the date that the explanation of the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity is provided to the Participant. However, the Participant's Annuity Starting Date may be before the date that any affirmative distribution election is made by the Participant and before the date that the distribution is permitted to commence under subsection (4) below; and

(D) A distribution in accordance with the affirmative election does not commence before the expiration of the 7-day period that begins the day after the explanation of the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity is provided to the Participant.
provisions.repairs: Joined the section number to its heading and removed list bullets; the blank line for a cross-reference is left as in the original.

provisions.name: 4.3 Optional Forms of Benefit
provisions.text:
4.3 Optional Forms of Benefit. In lieu of the Normal Form of Benefit or a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, a participant may, in accordance with such conditions or rules as the Committee shall prescribe and with the consent of the Participant's spouse, if applicable, elect any one of the following optional forms of benefit.

(A) Single Sum Equivalent - Subject to the elections and spousal consent requirements set forth in Section 4.2, a Participant whose employment has terminated and who is entitled to an Accrued Benefit may elect to have his Account Balance distributed to him in one lump sum as soon as is practical after the termination of his employment. However, in no case shall the Single Sum Equivalent be less than the Actuarial Equivalent of the Participant's Prior Accrued Benefit determined on the actuarial basis contained in Section 3.3. Furthermore, for any participant who qualifies for the special provisions of Section 3.8, the Single Sum Equivalent shall not be less than the sum of (i) the Participant's Prior Accrued Benefit determined on the actuarial basis contained in Section 3.3 and (ii) the Participant's Fresh Start Account Balance.

provisions.name: 4.4 Direct Transfer To An Eligible Retirement Plan
provisions.text:
4.4 Direct Transfer To An Eligible Retirement Plan. By direct payment of an Eligible Rollover Distribution to an Eligible Retirement Plan.

(A) Eligible Rollover Distribution. An Eligible Rollover Distribution is any distribution of all or any portion of the balance to the credit of the Distributee, except that an Eligible Rollover Distribution does not include: any distribution that is one of a series of substantially equal periodic payments (not less frequently than annually) made for the life (or life expectancy) of the Distributee or the joint lives (or joint life expectancies) of the Distributee and the Distributee's designated beneficiary, or for a specified period of ten years or more; any distribution to the extent such distribution is required under Section 401(a)(9) of the Code; and the portion of any distribution that is not includible in gross income (determined without regard to the exclusion for net unrealized appreciation with respect to employer securities).

(B) Eligible Retirement Plan. An Eligible Retirement Plan is an individual retirement account described in Section 408(a) of the Code, an individual retirement annuity described in Section 408(b) of the Code, an annuity plan described in Section 403(a) of the Code, or a qualified trust described in Section 401(a) of the Code, that accepts the Distributee's Eligible Rollover Distribution. However, in the case of an Eligible Rollover Distribution to the surviving spouse, an Eligible Retirement Plan is an individual retirement account or individual retirement annuity.

(C) Distributee. A Distributee includes an Employee or former Employee. In addition, the Employee's or former Employee's surviving spouse and the Employee's or former Employee's spouse or former spouse who is the alternate payee under a qualified domestic relations order, as defined in Section 414(p) of the Code, are Distributees with regard to the interest of the spouse or former spouse.

(D) Direct Rollover. A Direct Rollover is a payment by the Plan to the Eligible Retirement Plan specified by the Distributee.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined subsection (C) across a page break and removed list bullets.

provisions.name: Level Contingent Annuity (unnumbered, Article 4)
provisions.text: Level Contingent Annuity – A Participant may elect to receive his benefit in the form of an Actuarially Equivalent 50%, 75% or 100% level contingent annuitant pension. In no case shall the Level Contingent Annuity under this Plan be less than the corresponding level contingent annuitant benefit accrued under the Prior Plan with respect to his Prior Accrued Benefit. For purposes of determining the Level Contingent Annuity Form, Actuarial Equivalence shall be based on the Applicable Interest Rate and the mortality table prescribed by the Secretary of Treasury under Code Section 417(e)(3).

provisions.name: Level 5- or 10-Year Certain and Continuous Annuity (unnumbered, Article 4)
provisions.text: Level 5- or 10- Year Certain and Continuous Annuity – This form provides for Actuarially Equivalent monthly benefit payments for the life of the Participant and ceasing with the last monthly payment prior to his death. However, if fewer than 60 or 120 payments, respectively, have been made to the Participant prior to his death, the payments will be made to the Participant's Beneficiary until the total number of payments made to the Participant or his beneficiary equal 60 or 120, respectively. In no case shall the Level 5- or 10- Year Certain and Continuous Annuity under this Plan be less than the corresponding certain and continuous annuity accrued under the Prior Plan with respect to his Prior Accrued Benefit. For purposes of determining the Level 5- or 10- Year Certain and Continuous Annuity, Actuarial Equivalence shall be based on the Applicable Interest Rate and the mortality table prescribed by the Secretary of Treasury under Code Section 417(e)(3).

provisions.name: 4.5 Contingent Annuitant Factors
provisions.text: 4.5 Contingent Annuitant Factors. The 50% Contingent Annuitant Factor shall be equal to ninety percent (90%) minus one-half percent (1/2%) for each year the Contingent Annuitant's birthdate follows (or plus one-half percent (1/2%) for each year the contingent annuitant's birthdate precedes) the Participant's birthdate, to a maximum of fifteen (15) years.

provisions.name: 4.6 75% and 100% Contingent Annuitant Factors
provisions.text:
4.6 The 75% Contingent Annuitant Factor shall be equal to the 50% Contingent Annuitant Factor except that eighty-six percent (86%) and three-fourths percent (3/4%) shall be substituted for ninety percent (90%) and one-half percent (1/2%), respectively.

Similarly, the 100% Contingent Annuitant Factor shall be equal to the 50% Contingent Annuitant Factor except that eighty-two percent (82%) and one percent (1%) shall be substituted for ninety percent (90%) and one-half percent (1/2%), respectively.
provisions.repairs: The final paragraph appears struck through in the original; it is reproduced here as plain text, and the list bullet was removed.

provisions.name: 5.1 Pre-retirement Death Benefits
provisions.text:
5.1 Pre-retirement Death Benefits

(A) Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity. If a Participant dies before his benefits become payable and the Participant is married at the date of death, and has not elected an optional form of pension, a Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity shall be paid to the Participant's Spouse. Such Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity shall be equal to the Participant's nonforfeitable Accrued Benefit (determined in accordance with Section 6.2) and shall be paid in the manner described in Section 3.12(A). The Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity shall be payable as of the later of the first day of the month following the month of the Participant's death or the first day of the month following or coincident with the month in which the Participant would have reached his 55th birthday provided, however, that such Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity shall be reduced by the appropriate Early Retirement Factor for each month the Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity commencement date precedes the Participant's Normal Retirement Date. The Spouse may elect instead to receive the Participant's Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity in a Single Actuarially Equivalent Payment. For purposes of Section 5.1(A) the Single Actuarially Equivalent Payment is the greater of i) or ii) below.

i) An amount equal to the Single Sum Equivalent available to the Participant under Section 4.2, calculated as if the Participant had ceased employment on the Participant's date of death.

ii) An amount equal to the Pre-retirement Survivor Annuity multiplied by an Actuarial Equivalent factor. For purposes of this subsection ii), the Actuarial Equivalent factor is based on the Applicable Interest Rate, the Applicable Mortality Table, a benefit commencement date equal to the Participant's Normal Retirement Date, and the age of the Survivor at the determination date.

(B) Payment to Beneficiary. If the Participant dies before his benefits become payable and (1) the Participant was not married at the date of death or (2) the Participant is married but the Spouse has consented to the Beneficiary designation under Section 5.4, the Participant's nonforfeitable Accrued Benefit (determined in accordance with Section 6.2) shall be paid to the Participant's designated Beneficiary in an amount equal to the Single Sum Equivalent available to the Participant under Section 4.2, calculated as if the Participant had ceased employment on his date of death.
provisions.repairs: Joined the section number to its heading and removed markdown heading marks and list bullets.

provisions.name: 5.2 Disability Retirement Pension
provisions.text:
5.2 Disability Retirement Pension. A Participant who becomes Disabled while employed shall be eligible to receive a Disability Retirement Pension commencing on his Normal Retirement Date, which date shall be known as his Disability Retirement Date.

The Pension Committee may require proof of continued disability. Such proof may be required from time to time prior to his Normal Retirement Age, but not more frequently than once every six (6) months.

A Disabled Participant who has not commenced receiving benefit payments from this Plan shall accrue an amount of pension equal to his Yearly Accrual as determined in accordance with Section 3.8 for each Plan Year (including partial Plan Years) preceding his Disability Retirement Date during which he remains Disabled.

A Disabled Participant may elect to receive his Employee Derivable Accrued Benefit at any time prior to his Disability Retirement Date by filing an election to this effect with the Pension Committee.

provisions.name: 5.3 Contingent Annuitant Annuity
provisions.text:
5.3 Contingent Annuitant Annuity. The following additional provisions shall apply if the Participant is married at the time his pension becomes payable and the Participant's benefit is payable in either an escalating or level contingent annuitant form.

(A) A Participant may elect to waive the contingent annuitant annuity by filing the Plan form designated for that purpose with the Pension Committee within the 90 day period ending on the annuity starting date. The Participant's Spouse must consent to such waiver in the manner described in Section 5.5.

(B) The information described in (1), (2) and (3) below must be mailed or delivered to the Participant by the Pension Committee on or about 6 months before the Participant's earliest possible annuity starting date:

(1) The terms and conditions of the Contingent Annuitant annuity.

(2) The Participant's right to make, and the effect of, an election under Paragraph (C) to waive the contingent annuitant form of benefit.

(3) The rights of the Participant's Spouse under Section 5.5.

(4) The right to make, and the effect of, a revocation of an election under Paragraph (A).

(C) Any election made under this section may be revoked in writing during the specified election period, and after such election has been revoked, another election under this section may be made during the specific election period.
provisions.repairs: Paragraph (4) appears struck through in the original and is reproduced as plain text; list bullets removed and subsection (C) rejoined across a page break.

provisions.name: 5.4 Beneficiary Designation
provisions.text: 5.4 Beneficiary Designation. A Participant may designate any person or persons, including a trust, as his Beneficiary or contingent Beneficiary to receive his Accrued Benefit in the event of the Participant's death. Any such designation shall be made by filing the Plan form designated for that purpose with the Pension Committee. The Participant may change or cancel his Beneficiary designation at any time prior to death without the consent of any designated Beneficiary. If the Participant is married at the date of death, and the Beneficiary is someone other than the Participant's Spouse, the Beneficiary designation shall not be effective unless the Participant's Spouse has consented as described in Section 5.5.

provisions.name: 5.5 Consent of Spouse
provisions.text:
5.5 Consent of Spouse

(A) Any Beneficiary designation under Section 5.4 or waiver of the contingent annuitant annuity under Section 5.3(A) shall not take effect unless the surviving Spouse of the Participant has consented or consents to such designation or waiver, and the Spouse's consent acknowledges the effect of such designation or waiver. Any such consent must identify a specific alternate beneficiary and a specific alternate form of benefit payment. The consent shall be made on the Plan form designated for that purpose and must be witnessed by a notary public or Plan Official. Any such consent shall be effective only with respect to such Spouse and shall not be effective with respect to any subsequent Spouse to which the Participant becomes married.

(B) The consent of the Participant's Spouse shall not be required if it is established to the satisfaction of the Plan representative that the consent cannot be obtained because there is no Spouse, because the Spouse cannot be located, or because of such other circumstances as may be permitted under the Code.

provisions.name: 5.6 Post-retirement Death Benefits
provisions.text: 5.6 Post-retirement Death Benefits. If the total pension benefit payments to the retired Participant before his death and to any other person entitled to pension benefit payments after the retired Participant's death is less than the Employee's Contributions plus interest, the balance of such Employee's Contributions plus interest shall be paid to the Participant's Designated Beneficiary.

provisions.name: 6.1 Vested Benefit on termination of Employment
provisions.text:
6.1 A Participant whose Employment with the Employer or an Affiliated Entity terminates, other than by reason of disability or death, before his Normal Retirement Date shall be entitled to a Vested Benefit equal to 100% of his Employee Derivable Accrued Benefit plus a portion of his Employer Derivable Accrued Benefit multiplied by the vesting percentage as determined by the following vesting schedule:

Vesting Schedule
Completed Years of Service | Vested Benefit Percentage
Fewer than 5 | 0%
5 or more | 100%

In no event, however, shall a Participant's vesting percentage be less than his vesting percentage in a Prior Plan as of September 30, 1987.

Notwithstanding the above, the accrued benefits of a Participant of a Prior Plan that had a more rapid vesting schedule shall continue to vest under the provisions of the Prior Plan.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the opening sentence across a page break and reduced the markdown table to plain rows.

provisions.name: 6.2 Full vesting on disability or death
provisions.text: 6.2 A Participant who terminates from Employment with the Employer due to disability or death, shall be 100% vested in his Accrued Benefit regardless of his completed years of vesting Service.

provisions.name: 6.3 Payment of terminated Participant's Vested Benefit
provisions.text:
6.3 A terminated Participant's Vested Benefit may be payable in any of the optional forms as of any eligible Retirement Date. Furthermore, a terminated Participant may elect to receive his Vested Benefit prior to his earliest Retirement Date. Such terminated Participant may elect payment in the Normal Form or any optional form described in Article 4. For purposes of Section 6.3, the Single Life Annuity available to a Participant prior to his earliest Retirement Date is equal to the Participant's Accrued Benefit at Normal Retirement Date, actuarially reduced to the Participant's benefit commencement date via the Applicable Mortality Table. The Contingent Annuity Form and the Certain and Continuous Annuity available to the Participant under Section 6.3 are based on the Straight Life Annuity amount and the factors described in Article 4. If a Participant wishes to elect a single sum equivalent of the Participant's Accrued Benefit, the Participant may do so only if such single sum is transferred to a qualified plan (including but not limited to an individual retirement account) such that the Participant is not subject to current income taxation on any portion of the Participant's benefit. The Participant also may elect to receive his Employee Derivable Accrued Benefit at any time prior to his Normal Retirement Age by filing an election to this effect with the Pension Committee.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Prior Plan Benefits may be payable in any acceptable form in accordance with the provisions of the Prior Plan.
provisions.repairs: Removed a stray horizontal-rule page break between the two paragraphs.

provisions.name: 6.4 Change in Employment status
provisions.text: 6.4 A Participant who no longer meets the definition of "Employee" because of a change in Employment status but who remains in the employ of the Employer shall be entitled to receive a pension at Normal Retirement Date in the Normal Form equal to the yearly amount of pension determined in accordance with Sections 3.8 and 3.12 as though his date of change in Employment status were his Termination Date. Upon resuming his status as an Employee he shall again become a Participant hereunder as of the next Participation Date following his resumption of such status and his pension benefit at Normal Retirement Date shall be based upon both periods of service as a Participant hereunder. If such Employee should terminate Employment prior to his Normal Retirement Date and prior to the date on which he returns to the status of an Employee under this Plan, his termination benefit shall be determined in accordance with Sections 6.1 and 6.2 based upon his pension benefit as hereinbefore provided in this section.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break.

provisions.name: 6.5 Reemployment before Normal Retirement Date
provisions.text: 6.5 If a Participant whose service has been terminated under circumstances entitling him to a Vested Benefit is reemployed by the Employer before his Normal Retirement Date, the pension benefit to which he is entitled upon his subsequent retirement or other termination of service, shall be redetermined in accordance with the Plan; provided, however, that the years of Vesting Service of such Participant shall include the years of Vesting Service accumulated before such termination and all subsequent years of Vesting Service. His pension as so redetermined shall be reduced by amounts determined by the Pension Committee to be the Actuarial Equivalent of such pension benefits as may have been already paid to him under the Plan. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Participant who received a distribution which was less than the present value of his Accrued Benefit, and is reemployed by the Employer before his Normal Retirement Date, shall have his Accrued Benefit restored upon his repayment to the Plan of the full amount of the distribution, plus interest, compounded annually at the rate of 120 percent (120%) of the Federal mid-term rate as in effect under Section 1274 of the Code for the first month of the Plan Year in which the Participant repays the distribution. Such repayment must be made before the earlier of (i) five years from the date of reemployment, or (ii) the close of the first period of five consecutive One-Year Breaks in Service commencing after the distribution. Upon such repayment, a Participant who had been deemed to have received a distribution of his Employer-Derivable Accrued Benefit upon separation from service pursuant to Section 3.15(A), shall be treated as having repaid his deemed distribution. If the Participant does not repay the distribution within the period stated in the preceding sentence, then Years of Vesting Service prior to separation from service shall be disregarded. For purposes of Section 6.5, Actuarial Equivalent is based on the Applicable Interest Rate and the Applicable Mortality Table.

provisions.name: 6.6 Statement of rights on termination
provisions.text: 6.6 Upon termination of Employment of a Participant hereunder, the Pension Committee shall give to the terminated Employee, as soon as reasonably possible, a statement of his rights and benefits under the Plan arising because of such termination. Such statement shall include the amount of his Vested Benefit, if any, the time and manner in which such benefit may be paid and the procedure and action necessary on his part to receive such benefit. Such statement shall either be handed to the Participant prior to his last day of employment with the Employer or it shall be mailed to him at his last known mailing address.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 7.1 Employer responsibility for contributions
provisions.text: 7.1 The Employer shall have the sole responsibility for making the contributions necessary to provide the benefits of the Plan with respect to the Employees except to the extent that Employees are required to contribute to the Plan pursuant to Section 2.2. The annual Employer contributions shall be in amounts actuarially determined to be necessary to fund the pension benefits provided for the Participants.

provisions.name: 7.2 Actuarial computations
provisions.text: 7.2 Annually, or more frequently, the Employer or the Pension Committee shall obtain from an Enrolled Actuary, actuarial computations as to the minimum contribution necessary to fund the benefits provided by the Plan on an acceptable basis in accordance with Section 412 of the Code and shall certify such amount to the Employer. The Employer shall contribute to the Trustee and/or an insurance company such amounts as are deemed necessary by the Enrolled Actuary to fund the benefits provided by the Plan.

provisions.name: 7.3 Limitation of liability for benefits
provisions.text: 7.3 Except as otherwise provided by law, the benefits of the Plan shall be only such as can be provided by the assets of the Plan and there shall be no liability or obligation on the part of the Employer to make further contributions or payments in event of termination of the Plan. Also, except as otherwise provided by law, no liability for the payment of benefits under the Plan shall be imposed on the Employer, or its officers, directors or stockholders.

provisions.name: 7.4 Right to suspend or discontinue contributions
provisions.text: 7.4 Irrespective of any other provisions of this Plan, while the Employer hopes to maintain the Plan and to make the necessary contributions thereunder indefinitely, the Employer necessarily reserves the right to suspend, terminate or discontinue its contributions, in whole or in part, either permanently or temporarily, at any time. Any such discontinuation shall be by resolution of the Board and such resolution shall be notice to the Participants and to the appropriate Departments and Agencies of the Government as required in accordance with ERISA and the Regulations established thereunder.

provisions.name: 7.5 Exclusive benefit
provisions.text: 7.5 Except as provided in Sections 7.8 and 10.3 all Employer Contributions when made to the Plan and all property of the Plan including income from investments and all other sources, shall be retained for the exclusive benefit of Participants, Spouses, or their Beneficiaries and shall be used to pay benefits provided hereunder.

provisions.name: 7.6 Additional contributions
provisions.text: 7.6 The Employer may make in any calendar or fiscal year, any contributions under the Plan in any amount which is greater than the amount specified in Section 7.2.

provisions.name: 7.7 Discretion as to timing and amount
provisions.text: 7.7 The timing and amount of all contributions shall be entirely discretionary with the Employer to the extent permitted by law.

provisions.name: 7.8 Contributions conditioned on qualification
provisions.text: 7.8 All Employer contributions are made on the condition that the Plan shall receive a favorable determination from the Internal Revenue Service that the Plan meets the requirements of Section 401(a) of the Code and that such contributions are thereby deductible under Section 404 of the Code, and that such contributions are not based on a mistake of fact. If, and to the extent that a contribution was made based on a mistake of fact, or a favorable determination is not received, an amount equal to the Employer contributions so disallowed or the contribution so made shall be repaid by the Trustee to the Employer within one year after such disallowance or the date such contribution was made.

provisions.name: 7.9 Funding policy
provisions.text: 7.9 The Employer shall establish a funding policy and method to carry out the Plan objectives and shall periodically review such policy and method.

provisions.name: 7.10 Rollover contributions and direct transfers
provisions.text: 7.10 Subject to the approval of the Plan Administrator, an Employee, regardless of whether he or she is a Participant in the Plan, who has participated in a qualified retirement plan shall be permitted to make a rollover contribution or direct transfer to the Plan of the amount that is attributable to the Employee's participation in such other plan (reduced, in the case of a rollover contribution, by any nondeductible voluntary contributions he or she made to the plan). Before approving such direct transfer or rollover contribution, the Plan Administrator may request from the Employee or the Employee's prior employer, any documents which the Plan Administrator, in its discretion, deems necessary related to such transfer or rollover. Any direct transfer or rollover contribution to the Plan shall be fully vested and shall be credited to the Employee's Accrued Benefit under the Plan.

provisions.name: 7.11 Contributions for Employees relocated from Physicians Plus Medical Group
provisions.text: 7.11 The following provisions shall apply to Employees who cease employment with Physicians Plus Medical Group and become Employees of the Employer as the result of the mandatory relocation of the Employee's employment position from Physicians Plus Medical Group to the Employer. The Employer shall make an additional contribution to the Plan on behalf of each such Employee in an amount equal to the contribution that would have been made on behalf of the Employee to the Retirement Savings Plan of Physicians Plus Medical Group, S.C. for the Plan Year that includes the date of the Employee's mandatory relocation from Physicians Plus Medical Group to the Employer, attributable to the Employee's employment prior to the Employee's termination of employment with Physicians Plus Medical Group, if the Employee had continued employment with Physicians Plus Medical Group. Such additional contribution shall be added to the Employee's Accrued Benefit under the Plan, and shall be subject to the vesting rules otherwise applicable to Employer Contributions to the Plan.

provisions.name: 7.12 Contributions for Employees relocated from Physicians Plus Medical Group
provisions.text: 7.12 The following provisions shall apply to Employees who cease employment with Physicians Plus Medical Group and become Employees of the Employer as the result of the mandatory relocation of their employment positions from Physicians Plus Medical Group to the Employer. The Employer shall make an additional contribution to the Plan on behalf of each such Employee in an amount equal to the contribution that would have been made on behalf of the Employee to the Retirement Savings Plan of Physicians Plus Medical Group, S.C. for the Plan Year that includes the date of the Employee's mandatory relocation from Physicians Plus Medical Group to the Employer, attributable to the Employee's employment prior to the Employee's termination of employment with Physicians Plus Medical Group, if the Employee had continued employment with Physicians Plus Medical Group. Such additional contribution shall be added to the Employee's Accrued Benefit under the Plan, and shall be subject to the vesting rules otherwise applicable to Employer Contributions to the Plan.

provisions.name: 8.1 Pension Committee as Plan Administrator
provisions.text: 8.1 The Pension Committee shall be the Plan Administrator and shall be responsible for the administration of the Plan. The number of members of the Pension Committee, and the relative representation on the Committee of the Employer and the Affiliated Entities shall be determined by the Board of Directors of the Employer. The Pension Committee shall appoint a Chairman who shall be the agent upon whom legal process shall be served. A member of the Pension Committee shall not receive any compensation for his services as such.

provisions.name: 8.2 Resignation of Committee members
provisions.text: 8.2 Any one or more of the members of the Pension Committee may resign at any time upon delivery of a written notice of such resignation to the remaining members of the Committee, the Employer, and the Employer who appointed him to the Committee, the same to take effect not less than 30 days after the delivery thereof to the Employer unless the Employer agrees to accept a shorter notice.

provisions.name: 8.3 Removal of Committee members
provisions.text: 8.3 Any member of the Pension Committee may be removed by the Employer who appointed him to the Committee at any time. A certified copy of the resolution of the Board effectuating such removal, together with written notice of removal, shall be delivered to the member so removed and to the remaining members of the Committee, such removal to take effect at the date specified in such notice; provided, however, that no such removal shall become effective until all sums due such member for expenses incurred as a member of the Pension Committee shall have been paid to him.

provisions.name: 8.4 Successor Committee members
provisions.text: 8.4 If at any time one or more of the Pension Committee members or successor members, shall die, resign, or be removed, a successor member or members shall be appointed promptly by the Employer who appointed the member. Pending the appointment of a successor Pension Committee member or members, the remaining member or members shall have authority to act. Any successor or additional member shall signify his acceptance in writing to the Employer who appointed him.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 8.5 Meetings
provisions.text: 8.5 The Pension Committee shall hold meetings upon such notice, and at such place or places, and at such intervals as it may from time to time determine.

provisions.name: 8.6 Action by majority
provisions.text: 8.6 A majority of the members of the Pension Committee may perform all the duties and exercise all the powers imposed upon or granted to the members of the Pension Committee and every act and determination of a majority of the members of the Pension Committee shall be deemed to be and may be certified to be the act and determination of the members of the Pension Committee. The members of the Pension Committee or a majority of its members may act at a meeting or individually without a meeting. Any one of the Pension Committee members may perform any ministerial act not involving the exercise of judgment or discretion required of, or permitted to, the Pension Committee.

provisions.name: 8.7 Powers and duties of the Pension Committee
provisions.repairs: Rejoined subsection (E) across a page break and removed list bullets.

provisions.name: 8.8 Written instructions to the Trustee
provisions.text: 8.8 The Pension Committee shall, from time to time, issue written instructions to the Trustee with respect to the pensions and other benefits to be provided pursuant to this Plan.

provisions.name: 8.9 Certificate of Committee membership
provisions.text: 8.9 A certificate signed by the Secretary of the Employer certifying the names and signatures of the persons who are at the date of the certification members of the Pension Committee hereunder, and the Secretary of the Pension Committee, if any, shall be conclusive evidence for all purposes that such persons are the members of the Pension Committee and Secretary of the Pension Committee at the date of such certification, and on any date thereafter until a new certification is received, and that the signatures appearing are their authentic signatures.

provisions.name: 8.10 Authorization to sign; Secretary
provisions.text: 8.10 The Pension Committee may authorize one or more of its members to sign on its behalf any document relating to the administration of this Plan and, in its sole discretion, may appoint a person to act as Secretary to the Pension Committee, in which event the Secretary shall keep such records as may be necessary of the acts and resolutions of the Pension Committee, and may be delegated to perform all purely ministerial acts on behalf of the Pension Committee. In the event the Pension Committee authorizes one or more of its members to sign any document on its behalf as hereinabove provided, the Pension Committee shall certify such fact to the Trustee and shall keep it informed of any change in such authorization.

provisions.name: 8.11 Engagement of Enrolled Actuary
provisions.text: 8.11 The Pension Committee shall, in default of the Employer to do so, employ or engage an Enrolled Actuary to perform the functions described in Section 7.2, to recommend to them the mortality and other tables and the assumed interest rates to be used from time to time for any purpose of the Plan and to perform such other services deemed necessary or advisable in connection with the administration of the Plan.

provisions.name: 8.12 Reliance on experts
provisions.text: 8.12 The Committee will be entitled to rely conclusively upon all tables, valuations, certificates, opinions, and reports which will be furnished by any actuary, accountant, controller, counsel or other person who is employed or engaged for such purposes.

provisions.name: 8.13 Committee members as Participants
provisions.text: 8.13 No member of the Pension Committee shall be precluded from becoming a Participant under this Plan if he would otherwise be eligible.

provisions.name: 8.14 Abstention on own participation
provisions.text: 8.14 No member of the Pension Committee may act, vote, or otherwise influence, a decision of the Committee specifically relating to his own Participation under the Plan.

provisions.name: 8.15 Nondiscrimination in Committee action
provisions.text: 8.15 The Pension Committee shall not take any action in pursuance of the powers conferred herein which would be discriminatory in favor of Participants who are officers, shareholders, or highly compensated Employees, or which would result in benefiting one Participant or group of Participants at the expense of another or in discrimination as between Participants similarly situated or in the application of different rules to substantially similar sets of facts.

provisions.name: 8.16 Authority over Plan assets
provisions.text: 8.16 The Pension Committee shall have such authority with respect to the management of Plan assets as is granted to it by the Employer.

provisions.name: 8.17 Expenses of the Plan
provisions.text: 8.17 The reasonable expenses incident to the operation of the Plan, including the compensation of personnel employed pursuant to Section 8.7(E), shall be paid by the Pension Committee from the Trust Fund, unless paid by the Employer. Any such payment by the Employer shall not bind the Employer as to its right to elect, with respect to the same or other expenses at any time, to have such expenses paid from the Trust Fund.

provisions.name: 8.18 Claims and appeals procedure
provisions.text:
8.18 (A) Any Participant may file a written claim for a Plan benefit with the Pension Committee or with a person appointed by the Pension Committee to receive claims under the Plan.

(B) In the event of a denial or limitation of any benefit or payment due to or claimed by any Participant or beneficiary, such claimant shall be given a written notice setting forth the specific reason(s) for the denial or limitation of his benefit. The written notice shall include specific reference(s) to the Plan provision(s) on which the denial or limitation of benefits is based. In addition, it shall include a description of any additional material or information necessary for the claimant to perfect his claim; an explanation of why such material or information is necessary; and appropriate information as to the steps to be taken if the claimant wishes to submit his claim for review. This written notice shall be furnished to the claimant within 90 days after receipt of his claim by the Pension Committee unless special circumstances require an extension of time to process the claim. In the event of such an extension, a written notice of the extension specifying the reason(s) therefor shall be furnished to the claimant prior to the lapse of the initial 90-day period. In no event may the period for processing a claim be longer than 180 days, counted from the date of the original receipt of the claim.

(C) In the event of a denial or limitation of benefits, the claimant or his duly authorized representative shall be permitted to review pertinent documents and to submit to the Pension Committee issues and comments in writing. In addition, the claimant or his duly authorized representative may make a written request for a full and fair review of the claim, provided, however, that such written request for review must be received by the Pension Committee or by the person appointed to receive such requests within 60 days after receipt by the claimant of written notice of the denial or limitation of his claim. The 60-day requirement may be waived by the Pension Committee in appropriate cases.

(D) A decision shall be rendered by the Pension Committee within 60 days after the receipt of the request for review unless special circumstances make a longer period for decision necessary or appropriate. In such a case, a written notice of the postponement of the decision specifying the reason(s) therefor shall be furnished to the claimant prior to the lapse of the initial 60-day period. In no event shall a decision be rendered more than 120 days after the receipt of the request for review, except as described in Subsection (E).

(E) Notwithstanding Subsection (D), if the Pension Committee holds regularly scheduled meetings at least quarterly to review appeals, a claimant's request for review shall be acted upon at the meeting immediately following the receipt of the claimant's request for review unless such request is filed within 30 days preceding such meeting. In such a case, the request for review shall be acted upon no later than the date of the second meeting following the receipt of the request for review. If special circumstances (such as a need to hold a hearing) require a further extension of time, a decision shall be rendered not later than the third meeting following the receipt of the request for review, and written notice of the extension shall be furnished to the claimant prior to the commencement of the extension.

(F) Any decision made by the Pension Committee on an appeal shall be communicated to the claimant in writing in a manner calculated to be understood by the claimant. Such written decision shall set forth the specific reason(s) for the decision and shall cite the Plan provision(s) on which the decision is based.

(G) If a decision on a claim or an appeal is not rendered within the time specified in this section, such claim or appeal shall be deemed to be denied.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined subsection (C) across a page break and removed list bullets.

provisions.name: 8.19 Disputed payees
provisions.text: 8.19 If any dispute shall arise as to the persons to whom payment of any benefit shall be made, the Pension Committee may direct the withholding of such benefit until such dispute shall have been determined by a court of competent jurisdiction or settled by the parties concerned.

provisions.name: 8.20 Participant information
provisions.text: 8.20 Participants shall furnish promptly to the Pension Committee such information as the Pension Committee reasonably considers necessary or desirable for the purpose of administering the Plan. If such information is not submitted, or shows that such information previously has been misstated on the records of the Pension Committee, the Pension Committee will make such corrections and adjustments in accordance with the available facts as it considers appropriate.

provisions.name: 8.21 Employer records conclusive
provisions.text: 8.21 The regularly kept records of the Employer shall be conclusive and binding upon all persons with respect to the nature and length of Employment, the type and amount of compensation paid and the manner of payment thereof, the type of length of absence from work and all other matters contained therein relating to Employees.

provisions.name: 8.22 Records and annual report to Employer
provisions.text: 8.22 The Pension Committee shall keep full and complete records of the administration of the Plan. The Employer, acting through its duly authorized officers, Employers, or agents, may examine the books and records kept by the Pension Committee at any time. The Pension Committee shall render an annual report to the Employer within two (2) months after the end of each Plan Year, said report to be in such form and to contain such information concerning the Plan and the administration thereof by the Pension Committee as shall be requested in writing by the Employer and as may be required by the regulations of the Commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service or the Secretary of Labor or by any other appropriate department or agent of the government as required in accordance with ERISA and the Regulations established thereunder. The Pension Committee shall also render such further reports to the Employer as it may from time to time request of them. The Employer may designate auditors and/or actuaries to examine and audit the accounts of the Pension Committee.

provisions.name: 8.23 Participant access to records
provisions.text: 8.23 The Pension Committee shall during business hours make available to each Participant for examination by him, at the principal office of the Pension Committee, this Plan and such records as may pertain to the Participant. Any Participant may demand from the Plan Administrator a record signed by the Pension Committee of the Pension Committee's accounts with respect to his participation under the Plan, but he shall have no right to inquire as to accounts of other Participants.

provisions.name: 8.24 Annual report and retention of records
provisions.text: 8.24 The Pension Committee shall prepare, or cause to be prepared, an annual report for each Plan Year containing such financial statements, actuarial reports and other information in such form and for such delivery and availability at such times and in such manner, as may be required by ERISA and the Code and Regulations thereunder, and the Pension Committee shall retain such records for such periods as may be required by such laws and regulations.

provisions.name: 8.25 Mailing addresses
provisions.text: 8.25 Each person entitled to benefits hereunder shall file with the Pension Committee from time to time in writing his complete mailing address and each change of mailing address. Any check representing payment hereunder, and any communication, addressed to a Participant or to any other person at this last address so filed (or if no such address has been filed, then at his last address indicated on the records of the Employer) shall be deemed to have been received by such person for all purposes of the Plan, and the Pension Committee and the Employer shall not be obliged to search for or ascertain the location of any such person.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 8.26 Disclosure documents
provisions.text: 8.26 The Pension Committee shall furnish and make available to Participants and Beneficiaries, and to the Secretary of Labor or his delegate, to the Secretary of the Treasury or his delegate, and to the Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare or his delegate, such plan descriptions, summaries, reports, registration statements, notifications and other documents as may be required by ERISA and the Code, and Regulations thereunder.

provisions.name: 8.27 Payments to incapacitated Participants
provisions.text: 8.27 In the event that any Participant shall be physically or mentally incapable of receiving or acknowledging receipt of any payment due under the terms of this Plan and no legal representative shall have been appointed for him, the Pension Committee may direct any such payment to be made to an institution maintaining such Participant or to any relative by blood or marriage designated by such Participant as a Beneficiary or Contingent Annuitant for death benefits.

provisions.name: 8.28 Qualified military service
