provisions.text: 8.28 Notwithstanding any provision of this Plan to the contrary, effective as of December 12, 1994, contributions, benefits and service credits with respect to qualified military service shall be provided in accordance with Code section 414(u).

provisions.name: 9.1 Fiduciary duties
provisions.text:
9.1 In accordance with Title I, Section 404 of ERISA, any Fiduciary under the Plan, whether specifically designated or not, must:

(A) discharge all duties solely in the interest of Participants, Spouses and Beneficiaries and for the exclusive purpose of providing Plan benefits and defraying reasonable administrative expenses,

(B) discharge his responsibilities with the care, skill, prudence and diligence a prudent man would use in similar circumstances, and

(C) conform with the provisions of the Plan.

provisions.name: 9.2 Personal liability of Fiduciary
provisions.text: 9.2 A Fiduciary shall only be personally liable to the Plan to the extent required under federal and applicable regulations thereto.

provisions.name: 9.3 Prohibited transactions
provisions.text: 9.3 A Fiduciary must also refrain from engaging in any prohibited transactions as specified in Title I, Sections 406 and 408 of ERISA.

provisions.name: 9.4 Bonding
provisions.text: 9.4 In accordance with Title I, Section 412 of ERISA, any Fiduciary under the Plan and every "plan official" shall be bonded in the amounts and in accordance with the provisions of such section. The cost of providing such bond or bonds shall be considered expenses of the Plan.

provisions.name: 9.5 Indemnification
provisions.text: 9.5 The Employer shall indemnify the Pension Committee and any other person providing services to the Plan to the full extent of any expenses, penalties, damages or other pecuniary loss which may be suffered as a result of his responsibilities, obligations or duties in connection with the Plan or Fiduciary duties actually performed in connection with the Plan. Any amounts paid pursuant to such an agreement shall not be paid out of Plan assets. Such an agreement shall not relieve any person serving in a Fiduciary capacity of his Fiduciary responsibilities and liabilities to the Plan for breaches of any Fiduciary obligations.

provisions.name: 10.1 Amendment of the Plan
provisions.text:
10.1 The Employer, without the consent of any Participant, may amend this Plan at any time and from time to time by an instrument in writing executed in its name by an officer or officers duly authorized to execute such instrument and delivered to the Pension Committee; provided, however, that,

(A) No amendment shall provide for the use of funds or assets held under this Plan other than for the benefit of Employees and no contributions paid by the Employer shall ever revert to or be used or enjoyed by the Employer, except as provided in Section 10.3.

(B) No amendment shall adversely affect the rights accrued by any Participant prior to such amendment, nor shall it reduce or eliminate any early retirement pension or a retirement type subsidy, if any, (to be determined by Treasury Regulations) or an optional form of benefit payment.

Any such amendment shall be evidenced by a written instrument and upon delivery to the Pension Committee of such instrument, accompanied by a duly certified copy of the resolution of the Board of Directors of the Employer authorizing such amendment, this Plan shall be deemed to have been amended in the manner and to the extent therein set forth.

provisions.name: 10.2 Retroactive amendments
provisions.text: 10.2 Notwithstanding the foregoing, any modification or amendment of the Plan may be made retroactively, if necessary or appropriate to qualify or maintain the Plan as a plan meeting the requirements of the Code and ERISA, as now in effect or hereafter amended, or any other provisions of the law, as now in effect or hereafter amended or adopted, and any regulation issued thereunder.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the sentence split across a page break and removed the list bullet.

provisions.name: 10.3 Termination of the Plan and allocation of assets
provisions.text:
10.3 The Employer, without the consent of any Participant, may terminate this Plan at any time by an instrument in writing executed in the name of the Employer by an officer or officers duly authorized to execute such an instrument, and delivered to the Pension Committee. In such event the Pension Committee shall take the necessary steps to have all the funds held by the Trustee or an insurance company with respect to such Employer allocated to the extent that such funds are sufficient after providing for expenses of administration, in the following order of priority:

(A) An amount which will fund benefits that have been in pay status for the 3-year period before the termination of the plan or benefits the otherwise eligible Participants would have received if their benefits had begun at the start of such period, and were determined in accordance with Plan provisions in effect 5 years prior to the date of the Plan's termination.

(B) An amount which will provide an immediate or deferred retirement annuity with respect to all other benefits under the Plan which are guaranteed under the plan termination insurance provisions of ERISA as provided in Section 10.5.

(C) An amount which will provide an immediate or deferred retirement annuity with respect to all other nonforfeitable benefits under the Plan.

(D) An amount which will provide a deferred annuity Participants with respect to all other benefits under the Plan which are forfeitable.

If the assets of the Plan held by the Trustee or an insurance company for pension benefits for Participants of the Plan, as of the date the Plan is terminated, are not sufficient to provide in whole the amount required within the classes described above, such assets will be allocated pro rata within the class in which the amount first cannot be provided in full except that in the case of Class (C), allocation shall be done in accordance with Section 4044(b) of ERISA.

Allocation in any of the above listed categories is to be adjusted for any allocation already made to the Participant under a prior category. Allocation of assets may be modified by the Internal Revenue Service to meet nondiscrimination requirements. After all liabilities of the Plan have been satisfied, the Employer shall be entitled to any balance of the assets which shall remain.

provisions.name: 10.4 PBGC guaranteed benefits
provisions.text:
10.4 Amounts necessary to provide a Participant's guaranteed benefit up to the lesser of $2,642.05 per month (for 1977, adjusted for future changes by Federal Regulation) or 100% of average monthly wages during the Participant's highest five consecutive years in the Plan will be available through payments from the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation under the provisions of Title IV, Section 4022 of ERISA if the Plan assets are not sufficient.

Guaranteed benefits payable due to termination of the Plan within five years of its effective date or within five years of an increase in pension benefits shall be limited to the greater of 20% of the otherwise guaranteed benefit or benefit increase or $20 per month times the number of years the benefit or benefit increase has been in effect.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined "Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation" split across a page break and removed escapes before dollar signs.

provisions.name: 10.5 Merger or acquisition
provisions.text:
10.5 The Plan shall not be automatically terminated by the Employer's acquisition by or merger into any other Employer, but the Plan shall be continued after such merger provided the successor Employer agrees to continue the Plan. All rights to amend, modify, suspend, or terminate the Plan shall be transferred to the successor Employer, effective as of the date of the merger.

The merger or consolidation with, or transfer of assets and liabilities to any other qualified retirement Plan or Trust shall be permitted only if the benefit each Plan Participant would receive if the Plan were terminated immediately after such merger or consolidation, or transfer of assets and liabilities, would be at least as great as the benefit he would have received had the Plan been terminated immediately before any such transaction.

provisions.name: 10.6 Vesting on termination or partial termination
provisions.text: 10.6 Upon the termination or partial termination of the Plan the rights of all Participants affected thereby to the benefits accrued to the date of such termination or partial termination, are nonforfeitable to the extent then funded.

provisions.name: 10.7 Partial termination procedures
provisions.text: 10.7 In the event of a partial termination of the Plan, an appropriate portion of the funds held by the Trustee, or an insurance company, attributable to the Participants, Spouses, Contingent Annuitants and Beneficiaries subject to such partial termination shall be separated by the Trustee or insurance company with the aid and counsel of the Pension Committee, the Enrolled Actuary and the accountants for the Plan and in accordance with the applicable rules in ERISA or regulations thereunder and such partial termination shall become effective and such separate portion of the funds shall be allocated among the Participants and Beneficiaries subject to such partial termination in accordance with the provisions of Section 10.3.

provisions.name: 11.1 Restrictions on 25 highest-paid employees
provisions.text:
11.1 (A) Notwithstanding any other provision of the Plan, any Participant who, on any "commencement date," was among the 25 highest-paid employees of the Employer and whose anticipated annual pension under the Plan will exceed $1,500 shall not, in the event of the termination of the Plan during any 10-year period following such commencement date, be entitled to have used for his benefit an Employer contribution in an amount in excess of the greatest of the following four amounts:

(1) The Employer's contribution (or funds attributable thereto) which would have been applied to provide benefits for the Participant if the Plan as in effect on the day before such commencement date had been continued without change; or

(2) $20,000; or

(3) the sum of:

(a) the Employer's contributions (or funds attributable thereto) which would have been applied to provide benefits for the Participant under the Plan if it had been terminated the day before such commencement date, and

(b) an amount computed by multiplying the number of years for which current costs of the Plan are met after such commencement date by the lesser of:

(i) twenty percent (20%) of the Participant's annual compensation, or

(ii) $10,000; or

(4)

(a) if the Participant is a substantial owner (as defined below), the present value of the maximum benefit guaranteed for substantial owners under Section 4022 of ERISA if the Plan were deemed to be terminated on the date the benefit commenced;

(b) if the Participant is not a substantial owner, the present value of the maximum benefit described in Section 4022(b)(3)(B) of ERISA;

(c) for the purpose of this Paragraph (4), "substantial owner" shall mean an individual who, within 60 months of the date of reference, has owned, directly or indirectly, more than ten percent (10%) in value of either the voting stock or all stock of the Employer.

(B) The foregoing conditions shall not restrict the current payment of full benefits as provided in the Plan to any retired Participant while the Plan is in effect if (among other conditions) the benefits are to be paid in the form of level annuity payments.

(C) For the purpose of this section, a "commencement date" shall include the original effective date of the Plan and the effective date of any amendment to the Plan which increases benefits or extends benefits to individuals not previously covered by the Plan.

(D) This section shall not be interpreted to be in any way inconsistent with applicable regulations under the Code.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined the opening sentence across a page break, removed list bullets and escapes before dollar signs.

provisions.name: 11.2 Restrictions applicable to Highly Compensated Employees
provisions.text:
11.2

(A) In the event of the termination of the Plan during a Plan Year beginning after December 31, 1991, the restrictions on distributions contained in Section 11.1 shall be revised so that the benefit of any Highly Compensated Employee (and any Highly Compensated Former Employee) shall be limited to a benefit that is nondiscriminatory under Section 401(a)(4) of the Code.

(B) Annual payments to a Highly Compensated Employee or Highly Compensated Former Employee shall be restricted to an amount equal to the payments that would be made on behalf of the Employee under a single life annuity that is the actuarial equivalent of the sum of the Employee's Accrued Benefit and the Employee's other benefits under the Plan.

(C) The restrictions of Paragraph (B) shall not apply if (i) after payment to the Employee of all Plan benefits, the value of the Plan assets equals or exceeds 110% of the value of the current liabilities as defined in Section 412(1)(7) of the Code, or (ii) the value of the Plan benefits of the Employee is less than 1% of the current liabilities of the Plan.

provisions.name: 12.1 Exclusive benefit and qualification
provisions.text: 12.1 The Plan is created for the exclusive benefit of the Employees of the Employer, their Spouses and their Beneficiaries, and shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with its being a qualified pension plan as defined in Section 401(a) of the Code.

provisions.name: 12.2 No contract of employment
provisions.text: 12.2 This Plan shall not be construed as creating any contract of employment between the Employer and any of its Employees.

provisions.name: 12.3 Governing law
provisions.text: 12.3 To the extent not preempted by ERISA, this Plan shall be construed pursuant to the laws of the state where it is made and where it is to be enforced, which state is Wisconsin.

provisions.name: 12.4 Gender and number
provisions.text: 12.4 Wherever used in this instrument, the masculine gender shall include the feminine gender and the singular shall include the plural.

provisions.name: 12.5 Vesting on full or partial termination
provisions.text: 12.5 In the event this Plan is fully or partially terminated, all rights and benefits of Participants as herein provided shall then be fully vested to the extent funded.

provisions.name: 12.6 Severability
provisions.text: 12.6 In case any provision of this Plan shall be held illegal or invalid for any reason, such illegality or invalidity shall not affect the remaining parts of this Plan and this Plan shall be construed and enforced as if such illegal or invalid provisions had never been inserted herein.

provisions.name: 12.7 Misstatement of facts
provisions.text: 12.7 If it shall be found that the status of any Participant with respect to either his Employment or his Participation under this Plan, the age of a Participant or Contingent Annuitant or any relevant fact with respect to a Participant or Contingent Annuitant has been misstated, the amount of benefit shall be adjusted to what would have been payable on the basis of the correct information.

provisions.name: 12.8 Payments to minors or incompetents
provisions.text: 12.8 If a Participant, Contingent Annuitant or Beneficiary entitled to receive any benefits hereunder is a minor, or is deemed by the Pension Committee or is adjudged to be legally incapable of giving a valid receipt and discharge for such benefits, the benefits will be paid to such persons as the Pension Committee might designate or to the duly appointed guardian. Such payment shall, to the extent made, be deemed a complete discharge of any liability for such payment under this Plan.

provisions.name: 12.9 Nonalienation of benefits
provisions.text: 12.9 No benefit payable at any time under this Plan and no interest or expectancy herein shall be anticipated, assigned, or alienated by any Participant or beneficiary, or subject to attachment, garnishment, levy, execution, or other legal or equitable process, except for (a) a Federal tax levy made pursuant to Section 6331 of the Code and (b) any benefit payable pursuant to a domestic relations order which is determined to be a qualified domestic relations order as defined in the Code. Any attempt to alienate or assign a benefit hereunder, whether currently or hereafter payable, shall be void. No benefit shall in any manner be liable for or subject to the debts or liability of any Participant or Beneficiary. If any Participant or Beneficiary shall attempt to, or shall, alienate or assign his benefit under the Plan or any part thereof, or if by reason of his bankruptcy or other event happening at any time such benefit would devolve upon anyone else or would be enjoyed by him, then the Pension Committee may terminate payment of such benefit and hold or apply it to or for the benefit of the Participant or Beneficiary. In addition, the Plan shall offset a Participant's benefit under the Plan against an amount that the Participant is ordered or required to pay to the Plan with respect to a judgment, order or decree issued, or a settlement entered into, on or after August 5, 1997, pursuant to Code section 401(a)(13)(C) and (D).

provisions.name: 12.10 Distributions Under Qualified Domestic Relations Orders
provisions.text:
12.10 Distributions Under Qualified Domestic Relations Orders.

(A) Nothing contained in this Plan prevents the Trustee, in accordance with the direction of the Pension Committee, from complying with the provisions of a qualified domestic relations order as defined in Section 414(p) of the Code. This Plan specifically permits distribution to an alternate payee under a qualified domestic relations order at any time, irrespective of whether the Participant has attained his or her earliest retirement age (as defined under Section 414(p) of the Code) under the Plan. A distribution to an alternate payee prior to the Participant's attainment of earliest retirement age is available only if:

(1) The order specifies distribution at the time or permits an agreement between the Plan and the alternate payee to authorize an earlier distribution; and

(2) The alternate payee consents to any distribution occurring prior to the Participant's attainment of earliest retirement age.

Nothing in this section gives a Participant a right to receive distributions at a time not otherwise permitted under the Plan nor does it permit the alternate payee to receive a form of payment not otherwise permitted under the Plan.

(A) The Pension Committee shall establish reasonable procedures to determine the qualified status of a domestic relations order. Upon receiving a domestic relations order, the Pension Committee promptly shall notify the Participant and any alternate payee named in the order, in writing, of the receipt of the order and the Plan's procedures for determining the qualified status of the order. Within a reasonable period of time after receiving the domestic relations order, the Pension Committee shall determine the qualified status of the order and shall notify the Participant and the alternate payee, in writing, of its determination. The Pension Committee must provide notice under this section by mail to the individual's address specified in the domestic relations order, or in a manner consistent with Department of Labor regulations.

(B) If any portion of the Participant's Account is payable during the period the Pension Committee is making its determination of the qualified status of the domestic relations order, the Pension Committee shall make a separate accounting of the amounts payable. If the Pension Committee determines the order is a qualified domestic relations order within eighteen (18) months of the date amounts first are payable following receipt of the order, the Pension Committee shall direct the Trustee to distribute the payable amounts in accordance with the order. If the Pension Committee does not make its determination of the qualified status of the order within the 18-month determination period, the Pension Committee will direct the Trustee to distribute the payable amounts in the manner the Plan would distribute if the order did not exist and shall apply the order prospectively if the Pension Committee later determines the order is a qualified domestic relations order.

(C) To the extent it is not inconsistent with the provisions of the qualified domestic relations order, the Pension Committee may direct the Trustee to invest any partitioned amount in a segregated subaccount or separate account and to invest the account in Federally insured interest-bearing savings account(s) or time deposit(s) (or a combination of both), or in other fixed-income investments. A segregated subaccount remains a part of the Trust, but it alone shares in any income it earns, and it alone bears any expense or loss it incurs. The Trustee shall make any payments or distributions required under this Section by separate benefit checks or other separate distribution to the alternate payee(s).
provisions.repairs: Joined the section number to its heading, rejoined "18-month determination period" across a page break, and removed list bullets; the duplicated "(A)" lettering is as in the original.

provisions.name: 12.11 Condition of qualification
provisions.text: 12.11 Anything in the foregoing to the contrary notwithstanding, this Plan is established on the express condition that it will be considered by the Internal Revenue Service as a qualified plan under Section 401(a) of the Internal Revenue Code. In the event that the Internal Revenue Service determines that this Plan does not qualify under Section 401(a) of the Internal Revenue Code, this Plan shall be of no effect and the then value of any contributions made as a result of this Plan shall be returned to the Employer.

provisions.name: 13.1 General
provisions.text: 13.1 General. The following provisions shall apply automatically to the Plan and shall supersede any contrary provisions for each Plan Year in which the Plan is a Top-heavy Plan (as defined below). It is intended that this article shall be construed in accordance with the provisions of Section 416 of the Code.

provisions.name: 13.2 Definitions – introductory clause
provisions.text: 13.2 Definitions. The following definitions shall supplement those previously set forth in this Plan:

provisions.name: 13.2(A) "Aggregation Group"
provisions.text:
(A) "Aggregation Group" shall mean:

(1) each plan (including a frozen plan or a plan which has been terminated during the 60-month period ending on the Determination Date) of the Employer or an Affiliated Entity in which a Key Employee is a participant,

(2) each other plan (including a frozen plan or a plan which has been terminated during the 60-month period ending on the Determination Date) of the Employer or an Affiliated Entity which enables any plan in which a Key Employee participates to meet the requirements of Sections 401(a)(4) and 410 of the Code, and

(3) each other plan (including a frozen plan or a plan which has been terminated during the 60-month period ending on the Determination Date) of the Employer or an Affiliated Entity which is included by the Pension Committee if the Aggregation Group, including such a plan, would continue to meet the requirements of Section 401(a)(4) and 410 of the Code.

(4) solely for the purpose of determining if the Plan, or any other plan included in a required aggregation group of which this Plan is a part, is Top-Heavy (within the meaning of Section 416(g) of the Code) the Accrued Benefit of an Employee other than a Key Employee (within the meaning of Section 416(i)(1) of the Code) shall be determined under (i) the method, if any, that uniformly applies for accrual purposes under all plans maintained by the Affiliated Employers, or (ii) if there is no such method, as if such benefit accrued not more rapidly than the slowest accrual rate permitted under the fractional accrual rate of Section 411(b)(1)(C) of the Code.
provisions.repairs: Rejoined paragraph (2) across a page break and removed list bullets.

provisions.name: 13.2(B) "Determination Date"
provisions.text: (B) "Determination Date" shall mean the last day of the preceding Plan Year.

provisions.name: 13.2(C) "Key Employee"
provisions.text:
(C) "Key Employee" shall mean any Employee or former Employee who at any time during the 60-month period ending on the Determination Date is described below. "Key Employee" shall also include the beneficiaries of such persons. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the number of persons described in Paragraph (2) for the entire 60-month period shall be limited to 10.

(1) An officer of the Employer having annual compensation, as defined in Treasury Reg. §1.415-2(d), from the Employer and all Affiliated Entities for a Plan Year during such period greater than one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the amount in effect under Section 415(c)(1)(A) of the Code for such Plan Year.

(2) One of the 10 employees with annual compensation, as defined in Treasury Reg. §1.415-2(d), from the Employer and all Affiliated Entities greater than the amount described in Section 415(c)(1)(A) of the Code who own (or are considered as owning, within the meaning of Section 318 of the Code) the largest interest in the Employer or an Affiliated Entity, provided that such interest exceeds one-half percent (0.5%) of the total share ownership of the Employer or Affiliated Entity.

(3) A five-percent (5%) owner of the Employer.

(4) A one-percent (1%) owner of the Employer who has annual compensation, as defined in Treas. Reg. §1.415-2(d), from the Employer and all Affiliated Entities which, in the aggregate, is in excess of $150,000.

The above determination will be made in accordance with Section 416(i) of the Code. No more than 50 employees (or, if less, the greater of three employees or ten percent (10%) of the greatest number of employees, including leased employees within the meaning of Section 414(n) of the Code, employed by the Employer and all Affiliated Entities during the 60-month period ending on the Determination Date) shall be treated as officers.
provisions.repairs: Removed list bullets and the escape before the dollar sign.

provisions.name: 13.2(D) "Key Employee Ratio"
provisions.text:
(D) "Key Employee Ratio" shall mean the ratio for any Plan Year, calculated as of the Determination Date of such Plan Year, determined by comparing the amount described in Paragraph (1) with the amount described in Paragraph (2) after deducting from each such amount any portion thereof described in Paragraph (3).

(1) The sum of

(a) the present value of all accrued benefits of Key Employees under all qualified defined benefit plans included in the Aggregation Group,

(b) the balance in all of the accounts of Key Employees under all qualified defined contribution plans included in the Aggregation Group, and

(c) the amount distributed from all plans in such Aggregation Group to or on behalf of any Key Employee during the period of five Plan Years ending on the Determination Date, except benefits paid on account of death in excess of the accrued benefits or account balances immediately prior to death.

(2) The sum of

(a) the present value of all accrued benefits of all participants under all qualified defined benefit plans included in the Aggregation Group,

(b) the balances in all of the accounts of all participants under all qualified defined contribution plans included in the Aggregation Group, and

(c) the amounts distributed from all plans in such Aggregation Group to or on behalf of any participant during the period of five Plan Years ending on the Determination Date.

(3) The sum of

(a) all rollover contributions (or fund-to-fund transfers) to the Plan by an Employee after December 31, 1983 from a plan sponsored by an employer which is not the Employer or an Affiliated Entity;

(b) any amount that is included in Paragraphs (1) and (2) for a person who is a Non-Key Employee as to the Plan Year of reference but who was a Key Employee as to any earlier Plan Year; and

(c) for Plan Years beginning after December 31, 1984, any amount that is included in Paragraphs (1) and (2) for a person who has not performed any services for the Employer during the five-year period ending on the Determination Date.

(4) The present value of accrued benefits under all qualified defined benefit plans included in the Aggregation Group shall be determined on the basis of the assumptions described in Section 1.2.

provisions.name: 13.2(E) "Non-Key Employee"
provisions.text: (E) "Non-Key Employee" shall mean any person who is an Employee or a former Employee of the Employer or an Affiliated Entity in any Plan Year, but who is not a Key Employee as to that Plan Year. "Non-Key Employee" shall also include the beneficiaries of such persons.

provisions.name: 13.2(F) "Top-Heavy Compensation"
provisions.text: (F) "Top-Heavy Compensation" shall mean the average of a Participant's annual compensation (as defined in Treas. Reg. §1.415-2(d)) over the period of five consecutive Plan Years (or, if shorter, the longest period of consecutive Plan Years during which the Participant was in the employ of the Employer) yielding the highest average, disregarding (1) compensation paid in Plan Years ending prior to January 1, 1984 and (2) compensation paid in Plan Years after the close of the last Plan Year in which the Plan was a Top-Heavy Plan.

provisions.name: 13.2(G) "Top-Heavy Plan"
provisions.text: (G) "Top-Heavy Plan" shall mean each plan in an Aggregation Group if, as of the applicable Determination Date, the Key Employee Ratio exceeds sixty percent (60%), determined in accordance with Section 416 of the Code.

provisions.name: 13.2(H) "Year of Top-Heavy Service"
provisions.text: (H) "Year of Top-Heavy Service" shall mean any Plan Year in which a Participant completes 1,000 or more Hours of Service, excluding (1) Plan Years commencing prior to January 1, 1984 and (2) Plan Years commencing after the close of the last Plan Year in which the Plan was a Top-Heavy Plan.

provisions.name: 13.2(I) "Super Top-Heavy Plan"
provisions.text: (I) "Super Top-Heavy Plan" shall have the same meaning as Top-Heavy Plan except that ninety percent (90%) shall be substituted for sixty percent (60%).

provisions.name: 13.3 Minimum Benefit for Non-Key Employees
provisions.text:
13.3 Minimum Benefit for Non-Key Employees

(A) In each Plan Year in which the Plan is a Top-Heavy Plan, each Participant who is a Non-Key Employee (except a Participant who is a Non-Key Employee as to the Plan Year of reference but who was a Key Employee as to any earlier Plan Year) who has been credited with 1,000 or more Hours of Service during such Plan Year will receive a minimum Accrued Benefit. Such Accrued Benefit, when expressed as an annual benefit payable in the form of a single life annuity commencing at Normal Retirement Date, shall be not less than the lesser of:

(1) three percent (3%) of the Participant's Top-Heavy Compensation multiplied by the Participant's Years of Top-Heavy Service, or

(2) thirty percent (30%) of the Participant's Top-Heavy Compensation.

The minimum accrual applies even though under other Plan provisions the Participant would not otherwise be entitled to receive an accrual, or would have received a lesser accrual for the year because (i) the Non-Key Employee fails to make mandatory contributions to the Plan, (ii) the Non-Key Employee's Compensation is less than a stated amount, (iii) the Non-Key Employee is not employed on the last day of the accrual computation period or (iv) the Plan is integrated with Social Security.

(B) If a Non-Key Employee described in Subsection (A) participates in both a defined benefit plan and a defined contribution plan described in Section 13.2(A)(1) and (2), the Employer is not required to provide such Non-Key Employee with both the minimum benefit under this Plan and the minimum contribution under the defined contribution plan. In such event, the Non-Key Employee shall receive the minimum benefit described in this section, offset by the benefit provided by the defined contribution plan.

(C) The Minimum Accrued Benefit required (to the extent required to be nonforfeitable under Section 416(b) of the Code) may not be forfeited under Sections 411(a)(3)(B) or 411(a)(3)(D) of the Code.
provisions.repairs: Joined the section number to its heading and removed markdown heading marks and list bullets.

provisions.name: 13.4 Vesting
provisions.text:
13.4 Vesting

(A) Change in Schedule. Each Participant's vested interest in his Accrued Benefit shall be determined in accordance with the following schedule for any Plan Year in which the Plan is a Top-Heavy Plan, unless the vesting schedule previously set forth in the Plan provides more rapid vesting for such Participant:

Years of Service | Percent Vested
less than two years | 0%
two years | 20%
three years | 40%
four years | 60%
five years | 80%
six years | 100%

(B) Shift Out of Top-Heavy Status. If a Top-Heavy Plan ceases to be a Top-Heavy Plan, the vesting schedule previously set forth in the Plan shall again apply to all years of service. However, a Participant shall maintain the same vested interest in his Accrued Benefit determined under the schedule in Subsection (A) as of the date on which the Plan ceases to be a Top-Heavy Plan until the Participant's vested percentage under the schedule previously set forth in the Plan exceeds the percentage maintained under the schedule in Subsection (A).

(C) Special Election of Vesting Schedule. Each Participant with at least five years of service at the time that the Plan ceases to be a Top-Heavy Plan may elect to continue to have his vested percentage computed under the Plan in accordance with the vesting schedule set forth in Subsection (A). The period during which the election may be made shall commence on the date on which the Participant is informed that the Plan is no longer a Top-Heavy Plan and shall end 60 days thereafter.
provisions.repairs: Joined the section number to its heading, reduced the markdown table to plain rows, and removed list bullets.

provisions.name: 13.5 Compensation
provisions.text:
13.5 Compensation. If the Plan becomes a Top-Heavy Plan, the Annual Earnings of any Participant for purposes of accruing a benefit under the Plan for that Plan Year and all prior Plan Years of participation shall not exceed $200,000 (or such greater amount as may be prescribed by applicable governmental regulations). However, this will not result in the reduction of any Participant's Accrued Benefit determined as of the last day of the Plan Year before the Plan becomes a Top-Heavy Plan.

In the case of a Plan Year of duration shorter than 12 months in which the Plan is a Top-Heavy Plan, Annual Earnings shall exclude total taxable income of any Participant in excess of the amount determined by multiplying $200,000 (as adjusted) by a fraction, the numerator of which is the number of full calendar months occurring in such short Plan Year and the denominator of which is 12.
provisions.repairs: Joined the section number to its heading, rejoined the sentence split across a page break, and removed escapes before dollar signs.

provisions.name: 13.6 Social Security
provisions.text: 13.6 Social Security. For each Plan Year in which it is a Top-Heavy Plan the Plan must meet the requirements of this article without regard to any Social Security or similar contributions or benefits.

provisions.name: 13.7 Adjustment to Maximum Benefit Limitation
provisions.text: 13.7 Adjustment to Maximum Benefit Limitation. For each Plan Year in which the Plan is a Super Top-Heavy Plan, the 1.25 factor in the defined benefit and defined contribution fractions described in the "Maximum Benefit" provisions of the Plan shall be reduced to 1.0. The adjustment described in this subsection shall not apply to a Participant during any period in which the Participant earns no additional accrued benefit under any defined benefit plan and has no employer contributions, forfeitures, or voluntary nondeductible contributions allocated to his accounts under any defined contribution plan.

provisions.name: 13.8 Suspension of Benefits
provisions.text: 13.8 Suspension of Benefits. Notwithstanding the other provisions of the Plan, the payment of a Participant's Accrued Benefit shall not be suspended during the Participant's reemployment during any period in which the Plan is a Top-Heavy Plan.
